title: How to Use AI Tools to Learn Data Science Faster in 2026
abstract: How to Use AI Tools to Learn Data Science Faster in 2026 Discover how to combine AI assistants, coding tools, and adaptive platforms to cut your learning curve and build practical skills more efficiently. By Vinod Chugani on November 23, 2026 in Data Science Learning data science is more accessible now than it's ever been, and AI tools are a big reason why. Where students once spent days debugging a single script or searching through documentation, they can now get instant, context-aware explanations and code suggestions in seconds. But that accessibility comes with a catch. he best AI tools in 2026 reduce friction across the whole learning process. The best ones reduce friction across the entire learning process. The real question is which ones to use, and how to use them without letting them do all the thinking for you. The real question is which ones to use, and how to use them without letting them do all the thinking for you. This guide walks through practical strategies for using AI tools at every stage of data science learning, from building Python foundations to preparing for your first data science role. Getting the Foundation Right First Before reaching for any AI tool, there's one principle worth establishing: don't learn AI before you learn analytics fundamentals. This matters because AI assistants are most useful when you already have enough context to evaluate what they're telling you. If you ask an AI to explain a confusion matrix and you've never studied classification, the explanation will be surface-level at best and misleading at worst. Start by building a working knowledge of Python, basic statistics, and data manipulation with libraries like pandas and NumPy . Once you have that grounding, AI tools become multipliers rather than crutches. Use them to go deeper, not to skip steps. A solid starting point for structured learning is DataCamp , which offers an AI-native format with adaptive tutoring that adjusts to your skill level, pace, and context in real time. That kind of responsive feedback is especially useful early on, when misconceptions tend to compound if left uncorrected. Using AI Assistants as On-Demand Tutors With a foundation in place, conversational AI assistants become some of the most useful learning tools you have. Tools like ChatGPT and Copilot can answer coding questions, break down complex concepts, and generate code snippets on demand. No office hours, no waiting. The key is treating them as a thinking partner rather than a search engine. Instead of pasting an error and asking for a fix, describe what you were trying to accomplish, explain what you tried, and ask the assistant to walk you through what went wrong. That keeps you in the driver's seat while still getting the help you need. Three concrete techniques worth trying during self-study: Concept deep-dives. Ask the assistant to explain a concept multiple ways, then follow up until it clicks. If you're struggling with gradient descent, ask for a visual analogy, then ask how the learning rate affects convergence, then ask for a minimal Python implementation. Code review. Paste your own code and ask for feedback. Not just "is this correct?" but "what would an experienced data scientist change about this, and why?" Study planning. Share your current skill level and your learning goal (say, preparing for a machine learning role at a mid-size company) and ask the assistant to build a weekly study plan with specific resources and milestones. Accelerating Coding with AI Coding Assistants One of the biggest time sinks in learning data science is the gap between understanding a concept and being able to implement it cleanly in code. AI coding assistants close that gap. For learners specifically, the benefit isn't just speed. It's the ability to see idiomatic, well-structured code alongside your own attempts, which trains your eye for quality over time. GitHub Copilot is the most widely recommended option for data science contexts. Development teams using it report around 40% productivity gains on average, and for learners building portfolio projects, that speed translates directly into more finished work. That matters a lot for job seekers. Cursor is another tool gaining traction, particularly for developers who want tighter control over how AI suggestions are integrated into their workflow. When using a coding assistant for learning, don't accept every suggestion automatically. Treat each one as a prompt: do I understand why this code works? If not, ask the assistant to explain it line by line. That turns passive code generation into active learning. Here's a simple workflow for working through a new concept: # Step 1: Write your own attempt first import pandas as pd df = pd.read_csv('sales_data.csv') monthly = df.groupby('month')['revenue'].sum() print(monthly) This calculates monthly revenue totals from a sales dataset. # Step 2: Ask the assistant to suggest improvements # Copilot or ChatGPT might suggest: monthly = ( df.groupby('month')['revenue'] .sum() .reset_index() .rename(columns={'revenue': 'total_revenue'}) ) Comparing both versions and asking why the second approach is preferred builds intuition faster than tutorials alone. Building Projects with AI Guidance Portfolio projects are still the most effective way to demonstrate data science skills to employers. AI tools have made it easier to scope and execute them well. Most learners struggle more with direction than motivation. What dataset? What question? What level of complexity? AI assistants can help you answer all three, then serve as a sounding board as you build. A practical approach: describe your current skill level and target role to an AI assistant and ask it to suggest three portfolio project ideas that demonstrate relevant competencies. Once you pick one, ask it to help outline the project structure, including what exploratory data analysis to run, what models to try, and how to frame your findings. From there, use the assistant as you go. When you get stuck on a visualization, describe what you're trying to show and ask for suggestions. When model performance is lower than expected, ask for a systematic list of things to investigate. Jupyter Notebook remains the standard environment for this kind of exploratory work. Many AI assistants integrate directly with Jupyter through extensions, so you can get help without leaving your workflow. Using AI for Concept Reinforcement and Self-Testing One often-overlooked use of AI tools is active recall, one of the most well-supported learning techniques around. Instead of re-reading notes, ask an AI assistant to quiz you. A prompt like "Quiz me on the difference between bagging and boosting. Ask me five questions, one at a time, and tell me if my answer is correct before moving on" turns a passive review session into active retrieval practice. You can extend this to code challenges. Ask the assistant for a machine learning problem with a dataset description and expected output, then try to write the solution before asking for hints. This mirrors the format of technical interviews and builds both skill and confidence. For learners using Dataquest or similar interactive platforms, the browser-based coding exercises already build in this active practice model. Pairing them with an AI assistant for the moments you're genuinely stuck, rather than at the first sign of difficulty, gives you the best of both. Staying Current with Emerging Tools and Research Data science moves fast, and AI tools help you keep up with less effort. In 2026, the role of the data scientist has shifted from "model builder" to "AI orchestrator." That means learners need to understand not just classical machine learning methods but also how to work with large language models, build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and use frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex .

title: 5 Lightweight Alternatives to MCP for Giving AI Agents Tools
abstract: 5 Lightweight Alternatives to MCP for Giving AI Agents Tools Compare five lightweight ways to give AI agents tools without an MCP server, from a Python dispatcher to framework tools, REST adapters, subprocesses, and webhooks, and learn when MCP becomes worth adding. By Nahla Davies , KDnuggets on November 23, 2026 in Artificial Intelligence Suppose your application already has a function called lookup_product(sku) . The function reads one row from a catalog and returns a price. Now you want a model to be able to call it. Does that one lookup need a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server? Usually not, and it is worth being fair about why. MCP is a protocol for connecting tools to many hosts: a server describes its tools, and any compatible client can discover and call them. The current MCP architecture , the July 28, 2026 revision, runs over stdio on the same machine as well as over Streamable HTTP, so adopting it does not force a network service on you. KDnuggets' local MCP assistant walkthrough shows a complete system; here, we will compare how to connect one operation. The five options below are not five rival standards. They are five places the same function can live, chosen by what you already own: a few Python functions, an agent framework, a REST API, a command-line tool, or a workflow platform. Lightweight means fewer new integration and deployment responsibilities in the environment you have now, nothing more universal than that. Every example uses the same invented catalog. SKU BK-17 is an A5 field notebook at 1,299 cents in USD, and every record carries fixture: true so nobody mistakes it for a price list. The model in the live examples is qwen3.5:4b on Ollama 0.40.13, and every output shown is what the code printed. Keeping the Same Tool Contract Across the Five Choices Whichever connection you pick, three things happen in the same order. The model proposes a call: a tool name and arguments. The application checks that proposal against a contract it owns: the name must be one it allows, the arguments must fit the declared shape, and the operation must be one this user is permitted to run. Then an executor performs the work and returns either structured data or an explicit error, which the application passes back to the model. Figure 1. The application controls execution whichever connection it uses. Schematic of the five alternatives and the MCP lane they are compared with; no deployed system is depicted. Original diagram by Nahla Davies. The five alternatives change who the executor is and where the function runs. They do not change the business rule, and none of them removes the application's checks. OWASP's excessive-agency guidance separates three ways this goes wrong, too much functionality, too many permissions and too much autonomy, and all three are decided by the application, not by the transport. Existing component Connection choice Work that remains yours When the choice stops being simple A few local Python functions Native tool calling plus an allowlisted dispatcher Message handling, permissions and errors Several providers or clients need reusable contracts A Python agent framework Typed function tools Business authorization and dependency maintenance Framework coupling outweighs the saved glue A service with an HTTP interface A curated REST adapter, with OpenAPI as the map Credentials, allowed operations and response handling Broad or changing specs need a maintained adapter layer A trusted narrow command A bounded subprocess Argument policy, privileges and process failures Untrusted code or wider access needs real isolation A maintained workflow platform An authenticated webhook Workflow ownership, credentials and completion semantics Deploying the platform exceeds the saved integration work The contract itself is small: # catalog.py import re SKU_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{2}-\d{2,4}$") CATALOG = { "BK-17": {"sku": "BK-17", "name": "Field notebook, A5", "price_cents": 1299, "currency": "USD", "fixture": True}, "BK-18": {"sku": "BK-18", "name": "Field notebook, A4", "price_cents": 1799, "currency": "USD", "fixture": True}, } def validate_sku(sku: object) -> str: if not isinstance(sku, str) or not SKU_PATTERN.match(sku): raise ValueError(f"sku must match {SKU_PATTERN.pattern}, got {sku!r}") return sku def lookup_product(sku: str) -> dict: """Return the catalog record for one SKU, or raise KeyError if it does not exist.""" sku = validate_sku(sku) if sku not in CATALOG: raise KeyError(sku) return dict(CATALOG[sku]) 1. Use Native Tool Calling and a Small Dispatcher If the function lives in the same Python process as your model calls, the shortest route is the provider's own tool-calling interface and a dictionary. Ollama's native tool-calling exchange has three steps. You send the tool schema with the chat request, and the assistant message comes back with tool_calls instead of text. You run the call yourself and append a tool message holding the result. Then you ask again, and the model answers with the result in hand. # k1_native_tools.py (core) TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": { "name": "lookup_product", "description": "Look up one product in the catalog by SKU and return its price.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["sku"], "properties": {"sku": {"type": "string", "description": "Catalog SKU such as BK-17"}}}}}] DISPATCH = {"lookup_product": lookup_product} # a name not in here is never executed MAX_TURNS = 3 def run_tool_call(call: dict) -> str: name = call["function"]["name"] args = call["function"].get("arguments") or {} if name not in DISPATCH: return json.dumps({"error": f"tool {name!r} is not available"}) try: return json.dumps(DISPATCH[name](**args)) except (TypeError, ValueError) as err: return json.dumps({"error": f"invalid arguments: {err}"}) except KeyError as err: return json.dumps({"error": f"unknown sku {err.args[0]!r}"}) def ask(model: str, question: str) -> str: messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}] for turn in range(MAX_TURNS): reply = chat(model, messages)["message"] # POST /api/chat with tools=TOOLS, stream=False messages.append(reply) calls = reply.get("tool_calls") or [] if not calls: return reply.get("content", "").strip() for call in calls: result = run_tool_call(call) messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_name": call["function"]["name"], "content": result}) return f"unfinished after {MAX_TURNS} turns" $ python k1_native_tools.py --model qwen3.5:4b "How much is BK-17?" model proposed: lookup_product({"sku": "BK-17"}) application returned: {"sku": "BK-17", "name": "Field notebook, A5", "price_cents": 1299, "currency": "USD", "fixture": true} final answer: The price of the Field notebook (A5), SKU BK-17, is $12.99 USD. $ python k1_native_tools.py --model qwen3.5:4b "How much is BK-99?" model proposed: lookup_product({"sku": "BK-99"}) application returned: {"error": "unknown sku 'BK-99'"} final answer: I couldn't find the price for SKU BK-99 in our catalog. ... The dispatcher is the whole security model of this route, so it has to be a fixed dictionary, never getattr on a module or anything the model can name into existence. The second run shows why the error path matters. The model asked for a SKU that does not exist, and the application returned a structured error rather than raising. Given that error, the model told the user so instead of inventing a price. What this route does not give you is portability. The message shapes are Ollama's; a different provider has a different tool_calls layout, and you own the loop, the turn limit and every error. That is a fine trade for one application with a few functions and a poor one the day a second client wants the same tools. A tool function can be as thick as it needs to be behind that boundary. For a document-processing tool, extracting table data from PDFs can stay inside an SDK-backed function; the agent receives the returned fields rather than managing the PDF parser.

title: Working with AI
abstract: 01 Summary Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory Summary How are businesses across the economy adopting AI? What bottlenecks and challenges have they faced? How can employers reorganize human expertise around increasingly capable models? To understand businesses’ experiences better, we conducted 66 interviews with 58 of Anthropic’s enterprise customers. We found: Sources of AI value. Companies are deploying AI across a dizzying range of knowledge work tasks. In particular, they are increasingly using coding agents to bring software capabilities to nontechnical roles. Interviewees report that most uses of AI add value by increasing their output, rather than by cutting costs. They attribute this both to AI accelerating existing work and to its role in introducing novel product and service improvements. Impact on employment. Across our interviews, we saw very few examples of domestic layoffs that were driven by AI automation. Although some companies reported hiring more due to AI, most companies reported hiring less due to AI. Many also reported reducing their use of contractors, particularly offshore ones. These reported cuts could be an early warning of job disruption in the international business services industry. Bottlenecks. Companies reported a range of bottlenecks, including experts resisting AI deployment and tasks that are not accelerated by AI. As coding speeds up, for example, other tasks—like code review, sales, and strategic decision-making—increasingly need to keep pace. Limits to top-down and bottom-up approaches. Many companies approach AI by identifying a workflow to automate and rolling out a top-down solution. This approach can lead to job insecurity, fears of workplace surveillance, and resistance from the experts needed to set up an effective and durable workflow. Companies that distribute AI tools and wait for bottom-up adoption see some valuable AI use but face bottlenecks from unequal adoption and single-task AI implementations. Reorganizing for AI. Interviewees described the highest-value uses as involving meaningful reorganization. Some companies are broadening their employees’ roles to ensure individuals can take ownership over whole workflows, and are redeploying employees to the “bottleneck” tasks that AI models cannot do. Some also seek to empower employees by building out infrastructure to support nondeveloper coding and by providing broad-based internal access to business data. These companies are reorganizing to take advantage of ongoing model capability improvements rather than settling on a fixed approach that assumes AI tools will remain as powerful as they are today. Introduction The use of LLMs has exploded across the economy. How are human organizations reshaping around these strange new collaborators? Consider an employee at a midsize law firm that we spoke to. For years, the firm’s mailroom had followed the same protocol: a scanner sent PDFs of incoming correspondence to an inbox; a mail clerk opened each PDF, skimmed it, clicked “Save As,” renamed it, and placed it in the firm’s file system. The process took five minutes per letter. One day, a senior developer visited the mailroom to watch the mail being processed. In a month, he built an AI system that eventually became two API calls, which name the document based on its first page and then assign it a place in the firm’s document system. The mail clerks “were blown away.” An employee at another law firm we interviewed hoped AI would create “a second brain” for the firm. (“For higher-level stuff, it just opens up possibilities.”) But the firm struggled to get everyone to use AI effectively. Demand letters to potential defendants were filled with excessive em dashes and occasional errors. Attorneys building apps kept “running into the wall based on hallucinated menus or buttons that don’t exist.” Others worried about confidentiality and data security, or they just didn’t “have time to get onto this AI train.” A few power users inundated the firm with AI prose, “casually sending Claude-prompted seven-page instructions to the IT team.” A third law firm we spoke to adopted AI early and achieved strong uptake. One of the firm’s early projects was an AI timekeeping system that saved attorneys work tracking billable hours. IT staff saw parts of their job automated, but they then focused on building secure infrastructure to host apps and manage context that served the rest of the firm. As AI tools spread, the firm realized that associates were no longer needed to write first drafts of certain legal documents. But without writing, “how does an associate know if that’s a good draft or a bad draft?” So it introduced a new workflow where junior lawyers were “required to really take that first [AI-written] draft and work with a senior attorney,” pairing off and marking up and editing the draft together. These three firms applied the same technology in the same industry but in different ways. The first firm automated a workflow, creating efficiency gains but risking job displacement for the mail clerks. For the second, bottlenecks to adoption and effective implementation prevented job displacement but also blunted productivity gains that would benefit the firm. The third reorganized work without eliminating any jobs, because effective use of the technology required redeploying employees toward new tasks. The firm redesigned roles to maintain human expertise as a complement to increasingly capable AI models. In this article, we explore the connections between AI-driven value and work reorganization through 66 face-to-face interviews conducted across 58 companies in the US, all of which are in the midst of adopting AI. We interviewed executives, managers, and individual contributors. We talked to employees at AI-native startups and 100-year-old businesses. We interviewed people at manufacturers and tech companies. We spoke with structural engineers, dentists, and accountants; employees at hedge funds, law firms, and private equity firms; a property manager, a trucking company, and a publisher. They’re all Anthropic customers, but many also use other AI tools. They were selected for this study because of their range across industry, size, and AI usage, though they are not a random or systematically representative sample. As in other qualitative research, we present stories and a framework to organize them, with the expectation that follow-up quantitative research can test these ideas further. The interviews were done anonymously, both for the interviewees and their companies. Any names in the report are pseudonyms. How are businesses adapting to AI? In our interviews, we gained insight into how AI has become embedded in businesses across the economy. Some of the AI agents we heard about are sending faxes back and forth, as doctors’ offices refer and intake patients. Other agents are giving advice to technicians when an X-ray machine breaks, and still others are then marking up the X-rays to help patients better understand them. Agents are reading property deeds from the 1800s and working out delivery routes for gaming machines. Recently, an AI agent analyzed a company’s organizational chart and suggested departments where the company could add headcount: “Three heads here, we need to add two there, zero here.” Mostly, agents are writing code. Interviewees described 100 pieces of software that they wrote with AI in enough detail that we could categorize them. Eighty percent of this software automated previously manual work, like spreadsheet-based financial updates or taking meeting notes. Another 20% replaced existing software, often previously purchased from outside vendors. Agents are building apps for private parking enforcement, 401(k) audits, and trademark checks for new product names. They are making dashboards to track portfolio companies, equipment repairs, and debt collectors’ phone calls. How have human organizations harnessed these new assistants?

title: Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in beta
abstract: Over the past few months, we've been developing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) for our business customers. EFS provides state-of-the-art detection of sophisticated misuse, while remaining compatible with zero data retention (ZDR): neither Anthropic nor any cloud providers retain enterprises' data. Since we announced EFS in September , we've been developing it further with over 100 of our customers—including a quarter of the Fortune 100 and many companies in industries with strict rules on data visibility (like healthcare, financial services, and law). Leading enterprises like Bridgewater, Salesforce, and Stripe have been evaluating EFS in private beta. “As a company that runs critical infrastructure, safety matters as much to us as model capability. We need a solution that gives us strong safeguards while allowing us to keep our data in our own account. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards delivers just that.” Noopur Davis, EVP, Chief Information Security and Product Privacy Officer “At Stripe, protecting customer data is foundational to how we operate. Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards will enable us to use frontier models with added protection against misuse. It will also let us retain conversation logs in Stripe’s AWS environment, with access and review governed by Stripe’s security controls.” Matthew Kemelhar, Head of Security “With EFS, customers can keep sensitive data in their own environments, protected with their own encryption keys, while still preserving the specialized safety mechanisms frontier capabilities require. That balance, keeping enterprises in control of their data without abandoning frontier-model safety, is critical to broader adoption of advanced AI in security-sensitive organizations like Cisco.” Omar Santos, Distinguished Engineer “Enterprise Frontier Safeguards gives us exactly what we asked for: our logs stay in a Wells-managed environment under Wells-managed keys. We keep custody of our data while Anthropic operates the detection. That split is what lets our teams put frontier models to work safely and meet our obligations to customers, employees, and regulators. We helped shape these safeguards because our industry needs them.” Munish Kumar Sharma, Chief Information Security Officer “Where we have regulated or highly sensitive data, having Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with zero data retention will allow us to confidently accelerate our AI deployment across those highly regulated and sensitive client engagements.” Todd Lohr, US Vice Chair and Head of Client Technology & Innovation “As a company that runs critical infrastructure, safety matters as much to us as model capability. We need a solution that gives us strong safeguards while allowing us to keep our data in our own account. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards delivers just that.” Noopur Davis, EVP, Chief Information Security and Product Privacy Officer “At Stripe, protecting customer data is foundational to how we operate. Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards will enable us to use frontier models with added protection against misuse. It will also let us retain conversation logs in Stripe’s AWS environment, with access and review governed by Stripe’s security controls.” Matthew Kemelhar, Head of Security “With EFS, customers can keep sensitive data in their own environments, protected with their own encryption keys, while still preserving the specialized safety mechanisms frontier capabilities require. That balance, keeping enterprises in control of their data without abandoning frontier-model safety, is critical to broader adoption of advanced AI in security-sensitive organizations like Cisco.” Omar Santos, Distinguished Engineer “Enterprise Frontier Safeguards gives us exactly what we asked for: our logs stay in a Wells-managed environment under Wells-managed keys. We keep custody of our data while Anthropic operates the detection. That split is what lets our teams put frontier models to work safely and meet our obligations to customers, employees, and regulators. We helped shape these safeguards because our industry needs them.” Munish Kumar Sharma, Chief Information Security Officer “Where we have regulated or highly sensitive data, having Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with zero data retention will allow us to confidently accelerate our AI deployment across those highly regulated and sensitive client engagements.” Todd Lohr, US Vice Chair and Head of Client Technology & Innovation “As a company that runs critical infrastructure, safety matters as much to us as model capability. We need a solution that gives us strong safeguards while allowing us to keep our data in our own account. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards delivers just that.” Noopur Davis, EVP, Chief Information Security and Product Privacy Officer 1 / 5 Now, we're opening up EFS in public beta. In this post, we explain how EFS works in more detail, how it stays compatible with ZDR, and how businesses can join the beta program. How EFS provides automated safety monitoring with ZDR Customers who rely on legacy ZDR are protected by Claude's classifiers : our real-time safeguards that screen individual requests to assess whether they might cause harm. But sophisticated attacks generally occur across multiple queries—and any single request might, in isolation, look harmless. For example, our September threat intelligence report describes an operation against roughly fifty organizations in which an AI agent divided the work of an attack among many other agents running in parallel. It saved the credentials it had harvested between sessions, so that the attackers could easily resume their campaign. Viewed one request at a time, this attack would have appeared as separate, more benign tasks. To catch attacks like these, we use a second defensive layer, known as automated safety monitoring. This layer looks for patterns of misuse across many requests. Through EFS, Anthropic can provide automated safety monitoring without storing any customer data. Instead, our automated safety monitoring system analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by our customers. When automated safety monitoring finds a risk, it creates a Safety Case for you to review. These cases can be read from your cloud storage or through an API, and can be integrated with security information and event management systems. They do not include inputs and outputs. Once it's set up, automated safety monitoring can help your team detect intentional misuse that could lead to serious harm (like offensive cyber operations). It can also help detect agents that take actions beyond a user's intentions, such as—in extreme cases—using a software exploit to access an internal database or external system. Zero data retention and EFS With EFS, you bring your own storage for storing inputs and outputs. Neither Anthropic nor your cloud provider keeps a copy of your data once it is delivered to storage you control. This provides you the following guarantees: Zero data retention . Neither Anthropic nor your cloud provider retains your data. You bring your own storage and store your own data. Inputs and outputs are deleted promptly after they're written to your own storage. You configure your own access policies and audit logging, and encrypt safety data with your own keys. No operator human review. Neither Anthropic nor your cloud provider personnel access your inputs and outputs. Only automated safety monitoring can access this data. We never train on your data. Inputs and outputs are used only for automated safety monitoring, never for model or classifier training. You can use EFS through the Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, or Claude on Google Cloud. When you use EFS through Amazon Bedrock or Claude on Google Cloud (Google Managed), it's operated by your cloud provider, and the end-to-end data flow stays within that cloud's boundary.

title: KPMG's Todd Lohr on AI when your data is also your clients' data
abstract: KPMG is one of the world's largest professional services firms, with more than 276,000 employees providing audit, tax, and advisory services across 138 countries and territories. Todd Lohr, KPMG US Vice Chair and Head of Client Technology & Innovation, focuses on bringing AI to clients through products and platforms. He has worked on KPMG's AI capabilities for more than a decade. Much of the data KPMG handles belongs to its clients, often in highly regulated industries. Lohr spoke with us about what that means for adopting frontier AI, how embedding enterprise safeguards can unlock AI capabilities and accelerate responsible deployment, and where Enterprise Frontier Safeguards will fit. Why did KPMG decide to work with Anthropic? We’ve followed Anthropic very closely since its founding, and its mission was intriguing from a partnership perspective because we share a lot of the same values. At KPMG, trust is foundational. It's what clients expect from us across our core business of audit, tax, and advisory, and it's what underpins confidence in the capital markets. What are frontier models changing about your business right now? Ten years ago we were focused on using predictive analytics, machine learning, and bringing very bespoke applications of LLMs to our clients. The last three years have been marked by bringing general intelligence to both our clients and KPMG workforce. Now we're at another pivot point, where our strategy is to embed our industry and domain knowledge, like tax and legal, into AI platforms and products. We’re working with partners like Anthropic not only on how we help our clients disrupt their industries but also how we disrupt professional services more broadly. Our tax business runs on Digital Gateway (opens in new tab) , which we see as a market-leading platform for how we deliver services. With Claude now integrated into the platform, we’ve introduced Digital Gateway Powered by Claude (opens in new tab) , bringing frontier AI directly into how we work and deliver for clients with greater intelligence, speed, and scale. More capability means more value, but also more potential for misuse. How do you weigh the two? I’m optimistic about what AI can bring to humanity and to businesses, from healthcare and longevity to agriculture. We’re already seeing AI create entirely new ways to serve our clients in all industries. Healthcare is a good example. Emerging capabilities like ambient listening can generate clinician notes directly from patient conversations, and physicians tell us this type of tool could give them back hours each day. Clinicians remain firmly in the loop, and every hour they spend with patients rather than with systems is an hour that can improve care. With that said, the same technology can create security and safety challenges. There are going to be people who use it for nefarious reasons. It’s critically important that as an industry we understand that, take an honest look at how it’s being used, and create a responsible, safe, and secure framework for how we deploy these technologies. That’s why our Trusted AI framework (opens in new tab) is foundational to how we innovate at KPMG. As a professional services firm, we take seriously our responsibility to help organizations realize the value of AI safely and securely while preparing for what’s next. That includes rigorous testing, ongoing monitoring, human oversight, and independent assurance to help ensure AI systems remain transparent, reliable, and aligned to their intended purpose. Additionally, we're using Claude Mythos to identify system vulnerabilities, and cyber AI more broadly to defend against them.. This is an area where we’re investing heavily alongside partners like Anthropic. KPMG had an early look at Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (opens in new tab) . What was your reaction? It was positive to see how much thought and intention Anthropic put into the safeguards and working with partners on the program. Specifically, what stood out was data retention: how we will be able to keep the data within our organization and still have access to frontier models. That's critically important for a firm like KPMG because we are the trustee of our clients' data in some of the most sensitive, regulated environments. We want our clients and firm to have the benefit of the powerful combination of that data and AI, but we need to do it at all times in view of how our clients want us to use their data, and what we can use it for. What will Enterprise Frontier Safeguards let you do that you couldn't before? Enterprise Frontier Safeguards will allow us to move faster, with confidence, in how we're able to use AI and where we can use it. One of the key tenets of the safeguards architecture will be the ability for us to retain data in cloud infrastructure we control. Where we have regulated or highly sensitive data, having these safeguards built-in will allow us to confidently accelerate our AI deployment across those highly regulated and sensitive client engagements. How will the automated misuse review in Enterprise Frontier Safeguards fit with KPMG's own Trusted AI program and risk processes? As AI capabilities become more powerful and autonomous, organizations need the ability to identify potential misuse, emerging risks, and unintended outcomes at a scale that manual processes simply can't support. Automated misuse review helps provide that additional layer of oversight by continuously evaluating how AI systems are being used and flagging signs of serious misuse for our team to review. We see automated misuse review as a natural extension of our Trusted AI approach and an enhancement to our existing risk management processes. Combining automated monitoring, KPMG human oversight, governance controls, and independent assurance creates a stronger and more resilient framework than any one approach alone. What do you expect from AI vendors when it comes to safeguards? Trust is paramount to our brand. It's literally our business model. We’re not going to make a trade-off between AI capability and trust. We expect both. The more capable AI models become, the more important those safeguards become, and strong guardrails are what give organizations the confidence to put powerful AI to work at scale. We have an expectation with all of our vendors that safety, security, the safeguards around the use of AI, and alignment to our Trusted AI beliefs and programs are central to how we work together. We have to strongly prioritize safeguards in every aspect of our business, and certainly in our use of AI. What would you tell other leaders weighing frontier models right now? You need to use these models. I can't think of a business or an industry that is not going to have some level of disruption from AI. "Wait and see" is not likely a sustainable answer for most organizations. So, you have to adopt and secure at the same time. Think through the safety and security aspects, define the guardrails, and put them in place so you can move faster through the enterprise. Most organizations aren't going to have the luxury of not deploying these models. But they're going to have to do it in a way that's aligned to their business strategy and goals and done in a safe and secure manner. What are you building with Claude next? We've already started to put Claude to work to build AI-native ways of working in our business, specifically in tax and private equity. We've also built frontier AI cybersecurity services, and we’re using Claude Mythos to look at vulnerabilities across the enterprise, and then using AI to quickly patch and secure the enterprise against them. What you're going to see in the next several months is an acceleration effect. As AI enables organizations to identify vulnerabilities and risks faster, AI will also become increasingly important to responding at that same speed.

title: Introducing Claude Ship
abstract: Anyone who has opened a pull request knows how this goes. They start on the next thing, and then the review comes back. So they stop, dig back into the old code, push a fix, and wait for the review to run again. Then they go find someone to approve it. There's a good reason it works this way. Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that's easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code , and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too. That's why we built Claude Ship , available today in beta. It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what's ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it. Eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming. Claim by January 15, 2027. Terms apply. How Claude Ship works: review, fix, and approve Claude Ship is made up of Code Review , which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don't have to manage each step manually. Code Review performs an in-depth review of pull requests against the codebase through multiple lenses. It collects findings, adversarially verifies them, categorizes them, and posts them to a PR. On the Claude Code team, where Claude's review is one layer of a broader process, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the share reverted fell by more than 40%. Code Review gives teams fast reviews, clear findings, and a choice of Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels for each repository. PR Steward works to keep a PR green, but is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. It jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members. After every push, it comments with what it changed and how to undo it. Developers can comment @claude with an instruction to steer the work, or @claude stop to have it step back. From there, Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios. It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file. Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language. For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light. Two ways to get started For developers: /ship it from Claude Code Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code. When a change is ready, they run /ship . Claude pushes it, opens the PR, reviews the change, and works on feedback and failing checks to help get it ready to merge. What can merge depends on the developer's permissions and the repository's branch rules. For admins and engineering leaders: set the rules, one repository at a time Turning Claude Ship on for an entire repository puts it to work across a team's pull requests automatically, under settings and an approval policy the team controls. Developers don't need to manually invoke the /ship command. Admins choose where it runs. An admin turns on Code Review and PR Steward for each repository. Claude Approvals starts when a connected repository has a policy file on its default branch, and an admin can turn it off. Each repository gets the settings it needs. Admins choose the review level (Quick, Standard, or Deep), choose when reviews run, and configure spend limits. Teams keep the tools they have. Claude Ship works with existing branch protection and required checks. Teams set the pace. They can start with one repository, choose a review level and when reviews run, set a monthly spend limit, and run their approval policy in observe mode until they trust it. How the Claude Code team ships We run Claude Ship on many of our own pull requests. One of the biggest changes is who can act on customer feedback. For example, a product manager on the Claude Code team can now read a piece of feedback, talk through ideas and tradeoffs with Claude Tag, have it open a PR, and move on to the next thing while Claude Ship takes it through review, fixes, and an approval decision. Recently, a customer was confused because our Analytics API documentation implied an Admin key could pull Pro and Team usage. The PM asked Claude Tag whether a fix was in flight, and it opened one. Code Review found nothing blocking, a docs reviewer signed off, Claude Approvals passed, and the fix merged that same evening. What customers are saying “We have had numerous cases where Claude Code Review caught real issues before a human reviewer got to the pull request, and PR Steward helped the contributor fix them. Our reviewers were already using Claude Code to keep up with the volume, so having Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals start automatically when a pull request opens makes that simpler. We keep a human in the loop, and the human’s time now goes to the changes that need it.” Vatsal Bhatt, Director of Engineering “PR Steward is helping teams in our pilot spend less time working through code review feedback and more time building. We can tailor it to our teams’ processes, including how it suggests changes and organizes feedback. That flexibility has made it a useful part of the development workflow.” Alex Devkar, Senior Vice President, Engineering and Analytics Availability Claude Ship is available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available , and PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. Claude Ship usage is billed on tokens, so turning it on can add to an organization’s costs. The amount depends on the number and size of pull requests covered, the review level, how often reviews run, and how much work PR Steward does. Admins can set spend limits for Code Review and PR Steward. Claude Approvals has no base charge, but classifiers in a policy are billed on the tokens they use, and a policy that uses Claude's review triggers a billed Code Review, even in observe mode. Running /ship counts as regular Claude Code usage. Claude Ship is not available to organizations with Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys. Get started Developers can update Claude Code and run /ship on their next change. /ship is rolling out in Claude Code and the desktop app starting today. Teams already using Code Review can add PR Steward on a repository, and an approval policy in observe mode. Teams new to Code Review can read the setup guide to connect GitHub and turn on their first repository. Learn more in documentation .

title: The enterprise guide to securing coding agents
abstract: Shipping fast and secure Coding agents likely write code and open pull requests at your organization already. For many leading enterprises, they are reviewing, testing, and merging it too. For example, after standardizing on Claude Code across its engineering organization, Salesforce ¹ reported : 79% more pull requests merged per developer at Salesforce 5% fewer total incidents at Salesforce As agents do more, technical and security leaders must mitigate risks like prompt injection and privilege abuse with layered controls such as checked permissions and bounded environments. The first two chapters focus on scoping the risk. We discuss the requirements every AI provider should meet and four agentic risks to mitigate. The next three chapters focus on bounding the risk. We highlight the defensive layers you can deploy with Claude Code as well as how to centrally manage and enforce those controls. This guide aims to provide a helpful agent security framework that can give organizations the confidence and trust to run agents effectively at scale. The components of defending an AI agent: the model, the environment around it, and external checks on what goes in and what comes out. This guide is written for organizations on Claude Team and Enterprise plans. If you reach Claude through a cloud provider such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure, the same principles and local controls apply. 01 Setting the bar for agent security Six questions for every coding agent · Applying SaaS requirements to your AI provider “A CISO's responsibility in the age of agentic AI is not to achieve zero risk. Instead, our jobs are to make agentic risk legible and bounded. This way, we can deliberately accept what we can manage, so the business moves on our terms instead of around us.” Jason Clinton , Deputy CISO at Anthropic Six questions for every coding agent Here are six questions leaders can ask when evaluating coding agents to verify they are enterprise ready. Question to ask Why you should care Good answer Weak answer Does the model refuse when it should? The model is the first check on a harmful request, making a bad action less likely. Refusal trained into weights, with published rates. "Our system prompt instructs the model to decline." Are actions automatically inspected outside the model before they run? External checks can catch when the model is tricked or using bad judgment. Static analysis of commands and a separate evaluator model. Prompt injection probes. "The model is very capable." Is blast radius bounded by the environment? This bounds the severity, and therefore risk, of an incident. Kernel-level sandboxing that admins can require and set to fail closed, or an isolated VM for each session. Egress allowlisting at the network layer. "The agent is instructed not to leave the working directory." Can policy be locked centrally? Sets minimum standards that can’t be undone by individuals. Managed settings with hard-deny rules a local user can't override. “Per-developer config files, and an honor system policy doc.” Is the code the agent writes secure? Code volume is scaling and vulnerabilities can ship unless checks scale with the volume. Automated security review with a person approving high-risk changes. “The model is trained to write secure code.” Can you reconstruct an incident? Compliance. Improving security over time. Session telemetry export , audit API (Enterprise), and named known gaps. "Logs are available on request." Applying SaaS requirements to your AI provider You already have a SaaS provider checklist with controls such as single sign-on, role-based access, data handling terms, and audit logs. Hold AI providers to a similar checklist. For example, Claude Code supports these security expectations through: Single sign-on and role-based access control (Enterprise), managed the way you manage your other enterprise tools. We don’t train generative models on code or prompts under our commercial terms, unless your organization has chosen to share that data with us. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (rolling out in phases) combines the privacy of zero data retention with state-of-the-art safeguards for detecting misuse across highly capable models. Data can be encrypted with your own keys and kept in storage you control for a limited time. Learn more . On Enterprise, BAA coverage for the Claude Code CLI and the desktop app’s Code tab in local mode, once the HIPAA configuration is applied. Encryption options on cloud platforms: customer-managed keys in AWS KMS on Amazon Bedrock, CMEK on Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry’s Hosted on Azure option. A SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate in the Anthropic Trust Center . 02 Identifying AI-specific risks Leaked credentials and privilege abuse · Unvetted dependencies and extensions · Data exfiltration · Prompt injection Security and technical leaders are familiar with risks like leaked credentials, abused privileges, compromised dependencies, and insider threats. However the attack surfaces, velocity, and scale all change when it comes to agents. Let’s look at some of the risks. Risk How you handle it today What changes with an agent Leaked credentials and privilege abuse Least privilege, short-lived tokens, keyless auth through workload identity or OIDC. Regular review of over-privileged accounts. Named accounts for people, per-workload identity for software. Credentials should be short-lived and scoped to the task or job, not the developer’s full access. The agent acts inside a developer’s session and most logs outside Claude Code only show the developer’s name. Unvetted dependencies and extensions Pinned versions, review gates, two reviewers on manifest changes. Version controlled configuration. Agents add both vetted and unvetted dependencies faster than manual processes. Extensions instruct the agent the moment they connect. Data exfiltration Egress allowlisting at the network layer. A compromised agent can send data out through services you already allow. Unlike traditional malware, it can try multiple routes the attacker doesn’t have to proactively define. Insider risk Social engineering awareness training, verification, reporting paths. Prompt injection: The check moves to the tool call and the network boundary. Risk 1: Leaked credentials and privilege abuse Anything an agent can read, it can leak. That includes credentials like a long-lived AWS access key or GitHub token. Anything the agent can do, a compromised or overeager agent can misuse. By default, an agent in Claude Code runs under the identity of the developer who oversees it. In the event of an incident, you may need to distinguish between agent and developer actions so you can appropriately respond. Illustrative example of a pull request conversation. In the pipeline, the agent’s work arrives under its own name. Risk 2: Unvetted dependencies and extensions Agentic coding accelerates the rate at which code is generated and reviewed, which includes the speed at which dependencies are added and configuration changes are made. When you ask an agent to add JSON schema validation, it will find a package, add the latest version, and have working code in minutes. That speed can be a risk if agents aren’t pointed in the right direction. MCP servers, plugins, skills, subagent definitions, and a repository’s CLAUDE.md file are dependencies too, and they deserve the review you give a package. Unlike a compromised library, which waits to be called, they reach the agent as soon as they load. Their descriptions and instructions enter the context window before the agent has done any work. On Enterprise plans, skill and plugin scanning checks third-party skills and plugins for malicious content when someone uploads or edits them in your organization. Illustrative example of what an admin sees when skill and plugin scanning blocks a plugin on an Enterprise plan. Risk 3: Data exfiltration Every leak needs a route out.

title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab’s AI science benchmark
abstract: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. Chinese researchers optimize Huawei chips with a kernel improvement benchmark: …AscendGYM will help China do its own form of RSI… Researchers with the Shenzhen Loop Area Institute, a Chinese research organization, have built and released AscendGYM, “a kernel optimization benchmark for Ascend NPUs”. The purpose of AscendGYM is to make it easier to use AI to develop custom kernels for Ascend chips from Huawei – especially important given the export controls that prevent Chinese organizations from acquiring frontier Western semiconductors and forcing them onto Huawei. What AscendGYM does and contains: The goal is for AscendGYM to be the best way to evaluate the efficacy of AI-designed kernels as well as design new ones. The software is meant to help researchers answer this question: “Given a correct kernel implementation, can the specific agent further improve its performance for a target workload within an acceptable budget while preserving correctness?,” they write. “AscendGYM evaluates performance across multiple deployment cases, the best achievable performance for specific shapes and scenarios, and the optimization cost required to obtain these gains. Together, these dimensions characterize cross-case applicability, shape specialization, and optimization efficiency.” The software includes the AscendForge evaluation environment, which provides unified interfaces for “compilation, correctness checking, performance measurement, and feedback”. How well can AI models optimize Ascend chips? In tests, the single best model is Opus 5, followed by GPT-5.6, followed by GLM-5.3. They test out models in Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode; Claude Code yields the best absolute scores, and GLM does well in it, while GPT does well in Codex. Opus 5 is more token hungry and GPT-5.6 more token efficient. Why this matters – ingredients for Chinese RSI: For AI systems to be able to build themselves, they need to be able to develop and improve the software that is used for their own training and inference. Software like AscendGYM will be an essential ingredient for allowing China to rapidly improve the efficiency of its own compute substrates. The software will also have a bearing on export controls, where it provides a route to improve the performance of Chinese chips and close the gap with Western alternatives. Read more: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs (arXiv) . Get AscendGYM here : AscendGYM (GitHub) . Lawrence Livermore scientists test out if AI scientists can communicate uncertainty about experimental results: …Can AI systems be appropriately conservative?… “An agent that reports a confident wrong number is worse than one that reports honest uncertainty, because nobody downstream can tell the difference,” write researchers from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in a new paper that tests out how reliably AI systems can give accurate score ranges even when dealing with uncertainty. Testing for uncertainty: The paper introduces SciResearch-Eval, “an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material’s thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator”. The novel part of this eval is that “an agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth”. What they studied: They give AI agents a common materials science task – measuring a material’s thermal properties by heating a sample and fitting a heat-conduction model to its temperature response. “An agent receives a sample of unknown material, a simulator of heat conduction through it, one heating experiment, and budgets: four more experiments it designs, compute for simulations and fits, and a cap on actions. It must report the sample’s conductivity, heat capacity and rear heat-transfer coefficient with 95% intervals, and predict a measurement it may not run,” they write. “Hidden from the agent, the simulator may be under-resolved, physically wrong (the real sample has temperature-dependent conductivity, a glued joint, front-face radiation, or heat loss through its sides), or adequate but fed uninformative data”. Results – only the most powerful frontier models can do this : “When the simulator is missing real physics, only GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 are reliable at default settings; the Claude 5.5 models recover only at their highest reasoning setting, and older and open-weight models not at all.” These models are able to do well by automatically trying to measure where the simulator is accurate and where it is less accurate then bases their estimates on that, making them more resilient to the different ways the simulator gets broken in experiments. Why this matters – real scientists are careful, and so are powerful models: Papers like this are further indications that we’re entering an era of AI-driven science. Though many of today’s models can assist in scientific experiments, as this paper shows only a couple of the powerful models at the frontier are able to operate with such appropriate autonomous skepticism and inherent attendance to the scientific method that they can deal with unanticipated breaks in their equipment. This is both an indication of the science advancement to come and a sign of how the most powerful models are exhibiting more and more of an ability to generalize and make themselves robust to perturbations in their environment. Read more: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents (arXiv) . Check out the leaderboard here (official site) . Stanford professors launch AI startup that wants to create a world where thousands of models define the frontier: …Noeri sees two well-regarded AI researchers enter the neolab game… Stanford profs Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin have launched Noeri, “a neolab to push the frontier of plural intelligence”. They have raised $110m and are relatively light on technical details, but their main vision is that they want to create a world where the frontier is defined by powerful models which rely on the proprietary data of distinct organizations. “Rather than one monolithic source of truth, we can nurture many small, specialized intelligences, each tuned to a place, a people or a problem,” they write. Further details: “At Noeri, we are building intelligence that learns proactively and continually. Most AI today is trained once and then frozen, while the world it serves keeps moving,” they write. “We close that gap with living systems that grow out of our own research. Our work on test-time training showed that learning on the job after deployment can unlock new capabilities and lead to new discoveries. Our work on self-distillation found that a model can become its own teacher, learning from each mistake and solving hard problems in far fewer attempts. And our work on agentic orchestration demonstrated that a small model conducting a team of other models and tools can outperform frontier models at a fraction of the cost.” Why this matters – the political economy of the singularity: Currently, the dominant AI models are massive pre-trained ones from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI and a tiny handful of other companies. What would it mean for the frontier to be instead defined by a broader set of actors? This is a core question inherent to the political economy of AI and startups like this show how some people are going to try and utilize technical approaches to make that different vision a reality. Read more in the announcement tweet from Yejin (Yejin Choi, X) .

title: 實測：1450億參數塞進筆記本，每秒狂飆80+Token！國產端側大模型殺瘋了
abstract: 實測：1450億參數塞進筆記本，每秒狂飆80+Token！國產端側大模型殺瘋了 思邈 2026-11-23 19:01:15 來源： 量子位 零Token成本，斷網也能自由Vibe Coding 允中 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 上個月，曾經風靡全球的AI陪伴平臺Character.AI，申請了破產保護。 資料顯示，其月活躍使用者數（MAU）一度高達2200萬。破產時，在公司披露的經營困境中，核心因素之一就是 算力成本 。 這就出現了一個悖論： AI產品越成功，有時候反而越會帶來巨額虧損。 那有沒有可能，讓更多AI能力直接在本地執行，而不必事事依賴雲端？ 這正是端側AI近年來持續探索的方向。 但想把大模型真正搬到手機、PC等終端，並沒有那麼簡單。受限於裝置的視訊記憶體、記憶體頻寬、儲存和功耗，模型規模越大，越需要解決如何載入、如何排程，以及如何保證實際推理速度的問題。 行業急迫需要端側模型的進步。以蘋果此前公佈的3B參數端側基礎模型為例，其主要面向內容生成、摘要、分類和多輪對話等任務。蘋果當時也曾表示，這款模型並非為處理世界知識類問題或高階推理任務而設計。 此時，破局者出現了。 無界方舟近日釋出了端側大模型 Edge0-145B ，總參數量達到1450億，官方將其稱為「全球首個千億參數端側原生基礎模型」。 開源僅上線3天，便衝上了 Hugging Face的Text Generation榜單TOP 1 。 同時，該模型還在海外平臺Today’s News頁面中位列首位。 這個模型厲害的地方在於， 它突破了端側模型行業的智慧上限，還能在PC或高配筆記型電腦上執行。 在官方釋出的介紹影片中，Edge0-145B可以斷網Vibe Coding手搓小遊戲，且推理速度在80+ token/s。 咱們先來看看端側模型在這兩年的規模演進圖，雖然端側模型的參數被不斷推高，從1B到30B，但幾乎都停留在理論階段，硬體帶動不了。 從圖中可以看到，無界方舟第一次將端側模型拔高到千億參數水平 ，145B斷崖式領先。他們宣傳的特色就是「模型真正可用，不是實驗室裡的Demo」。 根據評測結果，145B參數的端側模型，智力水平已經可以對標雲端模型Claude Opus 4.6、DeepSeek-V4-Flash、Qwen3.8-Flash-Next等知名模型。對於長期以輕量化、小參數模型為主的端側領域而言，這也提供了一種新的技術探索方向。 這就意味著，它是一個可以Vibe Coding的端側模型，全程可斷網使用、無token費用。 斷網真能Vibe Coding 接下來，測試團隊按照官方公佈的配置要求，選用一臺NVIDIA RTX Spark筆記本進行實測。 裝置要求上，Edge0-145B最低可在配備12GB視訊記憶體、20GB系統記憶體的PC上執行，也支援配備48GB統一記憶體的Mac。 不得不說，曾經如果想把145B的雲端模型做私有化部署，還需要裝配180-300萬元的伺服器，現在僅需要約1.5萬元的筆記本就能流暢帶動。 團隊實測了三個案例，分別考察它在3D建模、遊戲製作和影片生成上的表現。 他們不止實測了Edge0-145B，還與雲端模型做了對比，來看看端側模型是否真的可以實現“比肩雲端模型”。 他們選擇了主流雲端模型GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 4.8進行對比。（沒有選擇Fable的理由，一方面是燒錢燒心，另一方面是沒幾個雲端模型可以跟它對打。） 實測1：3D建模（紐約時代廣場） 給了一段相同的prompt，讓Edge0-145B和主流雲端模型GPT-6 Astra、Claude Opus 4.8分別生成一個紐約時代廣場的三維場景。 任務要求： 在Blender裡搭建紐約時代廣場（Times Square）的當代夜景3D場景，並渲染一段20秒的穿梭飛越影片。鏡頭會在兩側佈滿LED廣告屏的“峽谷”裡低空穿行，依次貼近掠過多個標誌性景點，每個景點都要經得起近看。 說實話Edge0-145B的生成效果遠超預期，看起來和GPT-6 Astra不相上下，且這兩者都遠遠好於Claude Opus 4.8。團隊起初甚至以為把模型名字寫反了…… 大部分場景下，Edge0-145B和GPT-6 Astra難分上下，霓虹屏、街谷和高樓視窗都清晰可見，光影氛圍真實。 整體上看，GPT-6 Astra的氛圍更明亮一些，而Edge0-145B生成的霓虹廣告牌效果明顯優於兩個雲端模型，有更多設計感和視覺差異化。 實測2：遊戲製作（中世紀教堂） 在RPG-3D遊戲開發場景，同樣的任務和prompt，團隊也用三個模型做了對照。 任務要求： 為一款奇幻RPG遊戲搭建一個原創的中世紀主城場景：一座哥特式大教堂和它前面的城市廣場。做成遊戲宣傳片級別的3D場景，並渲染一段20秒的飛越影片。鏡頭會從老城上空俯衝到廣場，穿過大教堂主門洞，一路飛到中殿盡頭，每個景點都要經得起近看。場景是原創的虛構城市，不要復刻任何現有遊戲或影視作品裡的場景。 三個模型一對比，Claude Opus 4.8在細節的刻畫上略有欠缺。再看Edge0-145B和GPT-6 Astra，二者的產出效果十分接近。 在石板廣場的噴泉設計上，GPT-6 Astra生成的畫面更為精緻；而在教堂牆面的結構與細節方面，以及殿堂內部的彩色玻璃窗和拱頂的畫面上，Edge0-145B生成的效果都更好。 這些效果是在筆記型電腦上斷網跑出來的，全程沒有消耗任何token費用。 實測3：影片生成（機械原理科普） 為了呈現酷炫的效果，團隊讓三個模型用一套機器視覺檢測系統，把一臺渦輪噴氣發動機按照進氣道、壓氣機、燃燒室、渦輪和噴管拆開，並拆解標註各部分的執行溫度和零件編號。 任務要求： 做一段15秒的豎版產品動效短片：一臺渦輪噴氣發動機（turbojet）被一套“機器視覺檢測系統”拆開檢查，各段沿發動機軸向依次爆炸分離，螢幕上疊加追蹤框和英文標註，高溫段被熱場著色，然後重新裝好，最後落成一張乾淨的白底產品圖，並且首尾無縫迴圈。 在零件溫度的呈現上，Edge0-145B的熱色帶是深紫→品紅→琥珀→近白，熱色集中在燃燒室、渦輪和尾噴管，壓氣機保持溫熱狀態，更符合真實情況；而右邊Opus 4.8的生成效果沒有可讀的熱場圖例，標註文字也堆疊在了一起。 過去，這需要硬體工程師和三維設計師接力數天才能完成；現在，一臺高配筆記本在一個多小時內就能獨立交付。 從實測結果來看，Edge0-145B在部分任務上的表現，已經非常接近GPT-6 Astra等雲端模型。 更重要的是，在滿足配置要求的筆記型電腦上，Edge0-145B可以實現本地離線執行。 這意味著，使用者可以減少對雲端API的依賴，降低token呼叫成本。 對於政企、醫療、金融等對資料安全和隱私保護要求較高的行業，本地部署也提供了另一種AI使用方式，有助於減少敏感資料上傳雲端帶來的安全與合規壓力。 對於硬體廠商而言，裝載端側模型後，也可以拓展更多離線、弱網場景下的應用空間，進一步開啟海外市場。 “高智力端側模型的開創者”到底是誰？ 國產大模型Edge0，來自於創立僅兩年半的“無界方舟AutoArk”。 創始人曾曉東博士是MIT TR35獲獎者，也曾經是螞蟻技術實驗室的聯合創始人，曾主導支付寶盒、刷臉支付、無人超市等專案。 聯合創始人小喬，是今年Forbes福布斯華人精英TOP100入選者，個人獲得過37個國際獎項，涉及產品、設計、業務等不同領域。 團隊成員來自位元組、阿里、螞蟻、Google、Tesla、斯坦福、清華、復旦等知名企業與院校。 早在今年9月初，無界方舟就推出了 全球第一個可以在手機上流暢執行的35B端側模型：Edge0-35B 。 據介紹，這是全球範圍內，首次能讓一個350億參數的模型流暢地跑在手機上 。峰值記憶體不到2.5GB，在iPhone 18 Pro Max上的生成速度超過37 token/s。外網釋出帖的閱讀量在當天就突破了120萬，來自OpenAI、NVIDIA、高通等公司的多位技術專家和研究員紛紛轉發，模型也曾登上Hugging Face全站Trending榜第一。 他們同時開源了模型權重和統一推理框架，成為了端側企業和研究機構復刻的標準解法。此後，行業對端側模型的討論，從“幾十億參數”抬升到了350億參數這一檔。 而Edge0-145B的開源，代表著無界方舟在“探索端側智慧上限”這條路上又邁出了一大步。 與釋出同步，Edge0-145B在Hugging Face開放模型權重，全新的端側統一推理引擎在GitHub開源，並提供一鍵部署工具與完整硬體適配指南。釋出首日Day 0即全面支援macOS、Windows、Linux三大系統，覆蓋蘋果M系列晶片，以及NVIDIA RTX Spark、RTX 4090 / 5090等GPU平臺。 從1450億參數的模型架構，到配套推理引擎、部署工具和硬體適配方案，無界方舟正在探索一條面向實際終端應用的高智力端側模型路線。 全新技術路線，為端側而生 先來看看端側行業這兩年是怎麼卷的，主流思路就一個字：小。 模型一大，硬體就帶不動，所以端側模型的發展路徑從7B、3B，一路壓到1B，來換取更低的記憶體和功耗。代價是，參數越小，模型越笨。 以手機為例，端側模型的規格大多停留在3B左右，此類模型只能處理一些文案改寫、訊息提煉等簡單任務。 蘋果把on-device寫成Apple Intelligence的基石，更複雜、需要更大算力的請求再走Private Cloud Compute；谷歌提供可“優先端側、不行再上雲”的Hybrid Inference；微軟則寫下：“最豐富的AI體驗，只有雲和裝置一起工作時才可能。” 所以端側模型幾乎很難存在“小而美”。要麼“小而笨”，要麼“大到得上雲端”。 市面上，非手機和車機廠商推出的端側模型，即使把參數做小，仍面臨實際應用方面的挑戰，多數還停留在demo階段。 端側模型要 真正可用 ，得同時滿足五個條件： 記憶體裝得下、首字等得起、生成跟得上、功耗壓得住、長任務不變慢。 Edge0-145B交出的成績是： 記憶體裝得下： 視訊記憶體12G+記憶體20G以上即可流暢執行，也支援配備48GB統一記憶體的Mac。一臺中高階的個人筆記本或桌上型電腦就能執行，不需要伺服器； 首字等得起： 預填充（Prefill）速度1,100+token/s，幾十頁程式碼丟進去，第一個字即時出現； 生成跟得上： 解碼（Decode）速度80+token/s，比人的閱讀速度更快，不用盯著螢幕一個詞一個詞地等； 功耗壓得住： 典型功耗約80W，持續執行不降頻； 長任務不變慢： 支援128K–256K上下文，長文本下速度基本不衰減，長時間的複雜任務不會越跑越慢。 Edge0-145B的官網詳情頁，放了一張詳細的速度表： 以RTX 5090 D 24GB為例，NVFP4版本，智慧體解碼98.3 token/s，16K預填充3165.7 token/s；Q3_K版本更快一些，分別是121.2 token/s和3554.9 token/s。 Edge0-145B可以在滿足配置要求的筆記型電腦上流暢執行；Edge0-35B可以在手機上高速跑動。 這背後，無界方舟走了一條完全不同的技術路線：做 端側的原生基礎模型，且模型與推理框架協同設計與最佳化 ，而不是把雲端模型壓小。 關鍵在於， 它每次只調動其中一小部分參數。 據官網介紹，Edge0-145B採用 全新的潛空間稀疏MoE（Latent MoE）架構 ，把48層裡的專家全部重做 。 原來專家在2560維的寬空間裡算，現在先壓進一個窄空間（145B用1792維，120B用1280維）算，算完再還原回去。 一個專家從一大塊權重，變成固定1.63 MB的一條記錄，專家總參數145B少30%。 因為結構改了，所以他們用大量的資料重新訓了一輪，而且是直接按4 bit訓出來的，沒有在訓練後再壓縮。 另外，模型還搭配了一個全新的推理引擎 ， 視訊記憶體、記憶體、硬碟三級分層放權重。常用的專家留在視訊記憶體裡，不常用的按需搬進來，再加上投機解碼（一次猜幾個token再驗證）和雙卡協同。 能力上，除了團隊上面的實測可證明“端側智力首次比肩雲端”以外，也可以看看官方公佈的測試結果。 其中最亮眼的，要數 智慧體和程式設計 方面。 Terminal-Bench 2.1上，Edge0-145B拿下86.5，高於Qwen3.8-Flash-Next的83.3、DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731的82.7，也高於Claude Opus 4.6（Max）的78.2。 DeepSWE 1.1上，它拿到64.6，高於Flash-Next的58.7和DeepSeek的54.4。 產業佈局，是端側AI壁壘 從模型佈局來看，無界方舟成立兩年多來，已推出200+模型，其中覆蓋了端側大語言模型、語音模型、決策模型、向量模型等不同領域，充分滿足產業落地場景。 模型參數從0.1B到145B，可適配從機器人、PC、手機、筆記型電腦等中高配置硬體，到AI耳機、AI眼鏡、AI玩具等低配置硬體，每一檔都有對應的端側模型。 合作客戶包含多家知名消費硬體廠商，比如聯想、韶音、奇多多星球等；也有晶片類企業，比如地瓜機器人、高通等；此外還有多家AI軟體企業。 截至2026年10月， 企業客戶數已超過11萬家，包含大量由開源社群使用者轉化而來的頭部KA客戶 。 無界方舟的技術與產業落地，已經形成“飛輪”效應。 端側市場高度碎片化，不同晶片的NPU架構不同，對INT4、INT8、FP4等計算精度的支援各不相同，通用模型直接部署很難發揮硬體效能。 無界方舟具備從模型到推理引擎的深度調優能力，已適配95%的主流晶片平臺，如高通、恆玄、瑞芯微、全志、地瓜等，合作產業也覆蓋了耳機、眼鏡、手機、PC、機器人等各類硬體賽道。 端側會替代雲端嗎？ 多年來，端側模型都是雲端模型的補充和輔助，大眾也已經把AI得上雲端當作理所應當。 但如果端側模型已經可以對標雲端模型的表現，可以完成Vibe Coding等任務，成為生活和工作中的生產力，雲端便不再是唯一的答案，AI開始擁有更多走進日常工作和生活的方式。 使用端側模型，最顯著的好處有兩點：AI普惠、資料合規。 首先，AI不再有高昂的token成本。以一名開發者Vibe Coding為例，每天8小時約消耗1,000萬token，每月按22個工作日計，一年可以省下5-10萬元支出。 以B端企業為例，雲端token成本每年高達數百萬到幾十億不等，端側AI可降低90%以上的成本。 在純雲方案裡，AI是一項隨銷量增長而增加的成本；在端側方案裡，它變成了一項隨銷量增長而獲得的利潤。 第二，使用者隱私和企業資料合規都將有保障。端側模型將所有資料閉環在本地硬體中，資料不再上雲。可以放心讓端側AI讀取發票、財報、訂單和客戶資料，資料本地化是AI能在商業場景深度應用的前提。 在使用者和產業的需求上，token成本普惠、隱私合規有保障、斷網弱網可用，這些雲端模型的痛點剛好是端側模型的先天優勢。 未來，雲和端的邊界在哪裡？ 無界方舟表示： 有些事仍然需要雲端。如即時聯網搜尋、跨裝置的長期記憶。我們的目標是讓端側成為主力，而不是排斥雲端。 也就是說，消費者在日常生活和工作中使用的許多AI功能，大部分都可以通過端側模型解決。 以無界方舟的一個AI耳機品牌客戶為例，其產品使用的是端雲協同的解決方案，但已經有92%的AI使用是通過端側模型，僅8%通過雲端。 當端側智力水平與雲端齊平，硬體上手門檻進一步降低後，端側模型成為主力，似乎是不可撼動的趨勢。 而無界方舟，就是讓這個趨勢到來的變數。 傳送門： 無界方舟官網：https://www.autoarkai.com/model-detail/llm-145b Hugging Face： 145B模型：https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4 title: XROGO鄭隨兵：機器人不能只在影片裡，終究要進入工廠“真幹活”
abstract: XROGO鄭隨兵：機器人不能只在影片裡，終究要進入工廠“真幹活” 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-23 17:10:08 來源： 量子位 企業核心需求不是交付裝置，而是能持續上崗的勞動力 機器人越造越多，真正能“上崗“的卻不多。據《2026年人形機器人產業發展報告》，今年上半年我國人形機器人出貨量已超4萬臺；而一線調研顯示，超六成的具身智慧專案仍停留在驗證或演示階段，真正進產線連續、穩定作業的只是少數企業。 “這一現象背後是機器人部署成本高、換產難、長期穩定性不足等難題”。在近日舉行的 2026北京ACE科技創新大會上，XROGO CEO鄭隨兵指出，機器人能否持續在真實場景作業，正成為其關鍵價值所在。他表示“機器人終究是一種勞動力，不能只停留在影片裡，必須走進真實場景把活幹好、幹久。” 在鄭隨兵看來，當前行業真正缺的不是更多機器人，而是把活兒穩定幹完的作業能力。機器人的價值也並非去替代傳統自動化已能做好的事，而是把人的經驗、技能真正復刻出來。 行業缺的不只是機器人，而是“買得起、用得好”的勞動力 當前，製造業、電力、物流等行業普遍招工難、留人難。不少崗位環境艱苦：高噪音、高溫高溼、油汙粉塵，要熬嚴寒酷暑、上夜班、重複取放，企業常年貼著招工啟事，但很難招到人；配電室、變電站需要持證電工全天值守，冷庫、礦井、電線維護的工作時刻都暗藏風險；磨床操作、工件修型、火工品刮研這類活，高度依賴老師傅的經驗，人一走工藝就斷檔。 不僅如此，不同地域還存在巨大的成本落差。同樣的崗位，不同區域時薪差距懸殊，欠發達地區經濟體員工時薪顯著低於發達經濟體。一邊是“人不願來、留不住”，一邊是“成本壓不下去”，這構成了機器人最真實的應用理由。 有需求存在但不等於能被滿足。鄭隨兵指出，傳統工業自動化高度依賴整合部署，“佔地大、投入高，換一種工件，產線就要大改”，結果往往是“買了裝置用不起來”。機器人“部署”進了工廠，卻沒有真正“上崗”，這也解釋了行業為何一邊刷新出貨量新高，一邊在真實作業上進展遲緩。 作為聚焦建設全球勞動力基礎設施，打造全球勞動力呼叫與作業平臺的企業，XROGO第一步就是把機器人上崗門檻降下來，在真實場景裡“用得好”。在常州超級工廠等真實場景裡，機器人已在分料、揀選、推送和磨床操作等環節實現了100多個崗位的”真上崗“。操作一臺機床，插電、聯網到遠端部署約4分鐘，到崗計劃最快3小時。 鄭隨兵著重指出，“我們沒必要等到具身智慧達到100%完美，通過遠端協同和遙操兜底的方案也能讓機器人先作業起來。”一線工人不用寫任何程式碼可用自然語言告訴機器人該做什麼，並能通過遠端遙操的方式“幹活”，這一過程本身就是機器人學習的過程，實現人不在現場，也能瞭解注意事項、提前規避異常。機器人不再是焊死在產線上的固定裝置，而是能快速到崗、迅速切換任務、由一線人員帶教的“新勞動力”。 第二步就是“降成本”。要“像僱人一樣僱機器人”，可購機，可訂閱，也可按月租。XROGO在業界首次提出了“機器人到崗計劃”，首批開放50臺、免費4個月租金，可以從一個工位、一個任務開始試用。通過遠端遙操不同品牌的機器人，同時對接入的機器人嚴格把關，要求達到三年可靠無故障執行。XROGO機器人採用睿爾曼智慧自研的一體化關節模組，平均無故障執行時間達5萬小時，可支撐7×24小時連續作業。對企業而言，機器人“買得起、用得起”才能是規模化落地的關鍵。 機器人的價值在於復刻人類經驗，實現勞動力的全球排程 隨著全球老齡化加劇、用工成本上揚，“人在哪裡”與“活在哪裡”越來越難匹配，而機器人“真上崗”能夠更好地解決更深層的全球勞動力地域錯配的問題。對此，XROGO構建了“三端一腦”的遠端遙操協作模式。三端即勞動力端、平臺端、裝置端，一腦是指技能與模型。勞動力端可放在全球任何地點；裝置端放在成本高、招不來人、對人危險的地方，如配電室、變電站、礦井下、電線杆上、冷庫；平臺端負責勞動力排程；底層的“一腦”則是沉澱老師傅和遙操員的寶貴經驗。 以火工品修型、刮研這類高度依賴手藝的環節為例，老師傅的操作會被一次次學習、固化成技能包，再複用到不同機器人，形成資料閉環。人遠端操作約200至300次，機器人的成功率就可達80%以上，異常資料積累一週後反哺模型，成功率可迅速提升至95%乃至99%，之後人工的介入會越來越少。 同時這些技能與經驗也不再侷限於單臺裝置。一個機器人學會某種料箱的抓法，技能便會同步到雲端，供其他機器人呼叫；換一種工件也不必重做一遍產線。每一次遠端操作，都不只是為了完成當下的活，也在為減少人工介入、提升自主作業能力積累資料。 為檢驗機器人“真上崗”的價值，XROGO發起了“機器人真實作業與應用質量“的全球倡議。倡議提出四條機器人上崗的標準：參數求真、競爭求實；用真實應用檢驗模型；用長期作業檢驗質量；讓客戶收益檢驗價值。它不僅是份倡議，更是機器人規模上崗的“驗收標準”，看機器人能否規模上崗、持續工作，最終由付費客戶說了算。 未來機器人的下半場，比的不是零星部署在工作場景中的協作助手，而是能大規模在生產線上長期堅守工位、把一個個夜班頂下來、把一位位老師傅的手藝傳承下來，不斷創造價值的“勞動力”。 本文由XROGO提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 XROBO 具身智慧 機器人 量子位的朋友們 螞蟻阿福同款大模型宣佈開源，全球醫生一臺電腦就能解鎖專業醫療 title: 螞蟻醫療健康AI五連發！開源、本地部署、望聞問切全安排上了
abstract: 螞蟻醫療健康AI五連發！開源、本地部署、望聞問切全安排上了 鷺羽 2026-11-23 15:42:01 來源： 量子位 阿福大升級：讓模型像醫生一樣思考 鷺羽 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 我勒個豆，卷瘋了！ 一口氣連發五模型 …… 螞蟻百靈 這是要把醫療健康AI給穿透了。 一齣手，就是一整個模型大家族。 P.S.表格已經給大家整理好了，歡迎自取～ 還都是醫療深度推理、即時多模態互動以及疾病風險預測等硬核方向，精準踩中健康AI落地需求。 而且！前兩款專業模型，當天 直！接！開！源！ 不得不說，今年的螞蟻醫療健康生態大會，亮點多多，完全看不過來啊。 不妨先簡單梳理下這幾款模型。 開源的兩款模型體型差得還挺大： LingSante-3.1-air-VL：比較輕巧，只有124B，擅長處理報告、圖片這些圖文資料，適合本地部署； LingSante-3.1-flash：足足560B，最長支援100萬Token上下文，專門衝著長病歷和得來回查資料的複雜任務去的。 還有個普通使用者能輕鬆上手的 LingSante Live ： 開啟阿福APP，給AI打個影片電話，它就能直接 「望聞問切」 即時感知。 再算上識別疾病風險的 LingSante Pulse 、專門給醫療AI回答做安全保鏢的 LingSante MedGuard …… 阿福的技術老底都要被螞蟻全擺上桌了。 不止這些，螞蟻還給這一整套模型提了個更高的要求： 「模型要像醫生一樣思考」。 你品你細品，這可不是讓模型多背幾個醫學名詞就了事，是正兒八經要學會醫生的處事邏輯。 舉個例子，比如使用者說頭疼，一般模型可能羅列出一堆可能的疾病（嚇鼠了.GIF），但醫生式思考就會先問你疼了多久、怎麼個疼法，再決定下一步。 落到評測上，也要看模型推理過程是否完整嚴謹。 說白了，模型在醫療場景裡一點都不能馬虎。 So具體怎麼一回事呢？咱下面來把模型情況捋一遍，再真刀實槍實測跑一跑，你或許就能理解何為醫生思維了。 阿福一口氣亮出五大模型 你別說，最近我家裡人有個頭疼腦熱的，終於不來找我了。。。 扭頭都問起了某福。 倒也不算稀奇，阿福如今坐擁 1.5億使用者 ，單日就有近2000萬人次健康諮詢，其中 四分之一 還都是老年人。 現在拿份體檢報告問AI，已經越來越常態化。 但要光說報告裡那些向上向下的箭頭指標，阿福能解釋，其它通用大模型也未必做不到。 術語、參考範圍、可能的原因，幾秒鐘就能給你列得明明白白。 但 會解釋和能用 ，是兩碼事。 通用大模型最多會在末尾附一句建議就醫，反觀真正懂醫療流程的模型會更謹慎，也更重視潛在風險，在過程中就把 循證 做到位。 這樣使用者用得放心，醫生也能順手接住。 所以新一代健康AI真正要補的，其實是幾個聽起來並不性感的概念： 先追問再判斷，依據能追溯，邊界收得住，答完還能交給醫生複核。 圖片由AI生成 這事也不只是技術圈自己在較勁。 《國民健康「十五五」規劃》 提出從「以治病為中心」轉向「以健康為中心」，健康管理的重心往院外、往日常挪。AI要接住的場景，自然也要延伸。 這次集中亮相的五大模型，正好從不同地方切了進去。 LingSante-3.1-air-VL：解決醫療材料怎樣看得準 它也是阿福 首個 開源的多模態醫療大模型。 模型基於Ling-3.0-flash-VL構建， 原生支援圖文輸入 。總參數124B，得益於百靈底座的稀疏MoE架構，實際只用啟用5.5B。 之所以專門做這樣一款模型，有兩方面考量： 其一，恰恰因為很多健康問題，都是 從一張圖、一份文件開始的 。 使用者拍來一份體檢報告，往往就留下一句： 「元芳你怎麼看？」 。有時候吧，拍得還不完整，關鍵資訊差很多。 LingSante-3.1-air-VL要做的，就是讓一張圖成為繼續追問和查證的起點。在充分理解上下文資訊的同時，知道還 缺什麼 ，知道如何給出合理的建議。 為此，螞蟻還把醫學檢索和工具呼叫納入了設計，遇到問題先理解透徹再用工具動手解決。 另一方面，小參數設計節省的是推理時的計算開銷，對醫院來說，配上合適的硬體，就能又多一種 本地部署 的選擇： 讓病歷和檢查報告留在本地處理，減少敏感資料外傳。 這款模型的官方應用場景也比較豐富，不僅醫療專業能力突出， 通用能力 也沒落下。 除了能讀影像和體檢報告、分析皮膚照片和飲食圖片，也支援檢索醫學證據、輔助掛號購藥。 評測方面，整體醫療多模態能力穩居行業第一梯隊，尤其是影像報告生成與解讀、皮膚疾病識別、飲食營養分析、醫療報告解讀這幾項，均超過了 GPT-6.1 Sol 等通用模型， 位列第一 。 LingSante-3.1-flash：解決一摞病歷怎樣理得清 材料看懂了，下一步是把一堆專業材料理順，繼續做 醫療專業化 ，這是LingSante-3.1-flash的活。 它同樣用的是百靈當底座，基於Ling-3.1-flash構建。但總參數來到560B，沿用 Hybrid-linear MoE架構 後，長病歷、檢查報告、醫學文獻這些都能一口氣全塞進去。 此模型的訓練方法也值得多看兩眼。 團隊用了一套叫 ECM （證據—能力匹配）的辦法，先定要考的能力，再去病例報告、醫學考試等專業材料裡挖掘出合適的題目。 比如要練的是處理證據衝突，題裡就得有兩條不能直接畫等號的資料。 生成後的題目還要過一輪 多智慧體系統MEDPAR 檢查，看醫學事實有沒有問題、到底考沒考到預期的能力。 然後題目一部分用於監督微調，另一部分用於強化學習，雙管齊下讓模型既懂醫學又會分析病例。 訓練工具呼叫也是類似的思路，一次資料檢索做得怎麼樣，得看找回來的東西有沒有推進任務，然後再逐步最佳化搜尋步驟，減少無效搜尋和重複推理。 長程任務引入 多智慧體協作 ，也能進一步提升模型表現，比如BrowseComp準確率可以從91.33%推到93.84%。 另外團隊還注意到，在 程式碼執行 這類可驗證任務上做強化學習，醫學推理、專業知識檢索等能力也能跟著漲。 比如在一條程式碼強化學習訓練線上，TerminalBench從42.00到50.84，醫學知識推理從80.13到81.51，GPQA從77.78到83.33，搜尋聚合也從70.27到74.89。 最後通過 行為對齊 讓模型知道什麼時候該給出什麼樣的建議。 如果資訊不全，優先追問會改變判斷的關鍵細節；給出解釋時，分清已知事實和仍待核實的推測；遇到明確的危險訊號，及時提示就醫。 為此，團隊把不同任務與應遵循的專業行為交叉起來，為訓練題逐題制定評分標準。 最終，LingSante-3.1-flash在包含14項推理與安全對齊評測、19項Agent評測配置的綜合評測中，處於 開源領先水平 。 其中，HealthBench Professional得分高達 65.72% ，MentalHealthBench為54.64%，自建的中文公眾醫療諮詢測評集AFUMED-Behavior也有63.26%。 綜合得分61.21%，僅次於GPT-6 Astra，達成開源模型 SOTA 。 LingSante Live：從拍一張照片，到邊看邊聊 但光靜態的醫學材料還遠遠不夠，醫學面診講究的是 「望聞問切」 。 考慮到這點，LingSante Live來到了即時的你來我往： 打個影片電話，手裡的報告、藥盒，或者想讓AI看一眼的皮膚狀況，都可以對著鏡頭展示。 還能邊聊邊補，比如報告只露出了一部分，AI可以當場請你把手機往右挪一點。 它是面向健康協作的多模態互動架構，已經在阿福APP落地，選擇「視訊通話」就能實現AI 邊聽、邊看、邊說、邊做 ： 「望」是持續看畫面，並根據需要引導使用者展示更多資訊。 「聞」對應全雙工語音，系統在開口的同時還能繼續聽，使用者隨時可以插話。 「問」是系統綜合後臺分析結果，持續調整後續提問和引導。 「切」則是把感知範圍擴到音影片之外，探索結合非接觸測量與可穿戴裝置。 圖片由AI生成 綜合來看，模型把即時響應留在前臺，多源資訊持續進入系統，費時間的分析和規劃交給後臺Agent。 這樣使用者不必先把材料拍標準、把問題寫完整， 交流可以從眼下手頭這點資訊開始 ，模型會以更自然的方式逐步觀察獲取更多資訊。 LingSante Pulse：從日常生理訊號裡找疾病風險 不過還有一些健康問題，使用者未必已經察覺，更不會主動開口問。 LingSante Pulse瞄準的是生理訊號裡的 潛在風險 。 它能夠做150餘項的疾病風險預測，把關注點從已經發生的身體問題往前挪。 目前，團隊已經公開了生理訊號編碼器的權重，可以把心電等訊號轉換成供下游使用的特徵。具體疾病的風險預測，還需要配套的任務模型。 這次公開給開發者的，正是前面那一層 訊號處理能力 。 LingSante MedGuard：給醫療AI的回答做一次安全檢查 LingSante MedGuard則接過已經生成的醫療AI回答， 檢查裡面還有沒有風險 。 給了一個數值判斷，單位和計算對不對？引用的證據能不能支撐那句建議？ 團隊把這些檢查做進專門的防護模型，然後結合患者上下文，從 醫療安全、合規、倫理 三個維度挖掘隱蔽風險。 簡單來說，五個模型都是 順著健康問題發生的過程 在一步步拆。 單次諮詢裡，材料得讀懂、情況複雜了還得理順，缺的資訊可以在影片對話裡補，往前的日常風險要監控，往後也要給回答加一道安全閘。 百靈提供了圖文理解、長上下文和工具呼叫的起點，到了醫療場景，這些能力就開始各有側重。 但它們又並非完全孤立，彼此也能相輔相成， 組成更大的健康AI能力圖譜 。 至於這套分工在使用者手裡好不好用，上手試試就知道。 實測螞蟻阿福新模型 先來給LingSante-3.1-air-VL找個茬。 提供給它一份 血常規 檢測報告圖，但裁掉了單位和參考範圍，同時隱去血紅蛋白和紅細胞計數的結果，問它如何看待這份報告。 同樣的問題，我也丟給了 GPT-6.2 Sol 。 二者的生成速度差不多，都是在思考十秒左右給出的結果。 但LingSante-3.1-air-VL比較謹慎，在發現關鍵證據血紅蛋白缺失的情況下， 沒有給出明確的結論 。 反觀GPT-6.2 Sol，直接開頭給出了中度缺鐵性貧血的結果，在列指標時，也完全忽略了血紅蛋白情況。 再往下看，兩個模型對血紅蛋白的處理也發生了明顯分歧： LingSante-3.1-air-VL會明確建議 下一輪互動補充相關數值 ，GPT-6.2 Sol直接用其它指標反推估算。 雖然這樣做在數學上自洽，但在後續流程中極易將近似值當作真實檢驗資料，存在誤導臨床決策的隱患。 LingSante-3.1-air-VL更為保守安全，循證性強， 符合醫療SOP 。 第二輪我們再將完整的報告截圖，同時發給兩個模型。 在貧血型別的鑑別上，二者均利用新增數值計算了Mentzer指數（MCV ÷ RBC），給出了進一步的「優先排除地中海貧血」的結論。 但在後續的建議中，LingSante-3.1-air-VL明顯更面面俱到，包括從後續檢測、溯源、治療、隨訪、飲食到危險預警的整條鏈路， 面向患者友好 。 切換到 LingSante-3.1-flash ，題目改成低鈉血癥的病因歸屬，每一個數據點都在逼迫模型做真正的證據權衡，集中考驗模型的知識推理能力。 這一次模型輸出時間較長，但整體來說，結構相當完整，箇中判斷精準且有理有據。 第一層 分類 ，LingSante-3.1-flash基本滿分通過，低滲性分類正確，假性低鈉與高滲性干擾覆蓋完整，還提到了額外的滲透隙。 第二層 鑑別 ，也是模型醫生思維體現最明顯的地方。 它沒有把「尿鈉高+血尿酸低」當成SIADH（抗利尿激素分泌不當綜合徵）的明確證據，而且主動否決了這兩項的鑑別力。這恰恰是那些背結論的模型最容易翻車的地方，但LingSante-3.1-flash規避掉了。 第三層 處置 ，方向也是全對的，但給出的糾正速率閾值（高危者24h≤4–6mmol/L、48h ≤8–12mmol/L）過度保守，並非指南推薦值（高危者24h≤8mmol/L、48h ≤18mmol/L）。 第四層 證據層級 ，模型表現誠實且分層清楚，其中把「容量狀態與補鹽反應」標註為弱推薦、經驗性判斷最大的環節，說明它的推理多於背答案。 同樣是交給GPT，對比下來，還是LingSante-3.1-flash 組織知識的完整性與可讀性更高 ，GPT-6.2 Sol的執行層與判斷層存在脫鉤的情況。 GPT-6.2 Sol也有值得學習的地方，比如文內生成有 結構圖 輔助理解。 最後我們再在阿福APP上體驗 LingSante Live 的視訊通話功能。 先給遠景，模型精準識別出藥品名稱及型別，並建議下一步拉近鏡頭距離，好看清成分那一欄。 影片連結：https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ceH1mQR_6BNAlI5l2ehF7w 鏡頭拉近後，LingSante Live還會 接著和使用者聊 ，哪裡沒看清，就提示使用者再調一下藥品位置，直到看清需要核對的資訊。 即使是小語種文字，LingSante Live也很快就翻譯了出來。 中途插話打斷 ，它也能馬上接住，順著新問題往下聊。 影片連結：https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ceH1mQR_6BNAlI5l2ehF7w 模擬給一些突發狀況，比如外用藥誤食或者入眼，LingSante Live也能根據藥物成分合理給出 即時建議 。 影片連結：https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ceH1mQR_6BNAlI5l2ehF7w 也試了試影片面診。萬萬沒想到，聊著聊著，它還會主動嘗試估測我的呼吸頻次和即時心率。看到鏡頭裡的皮膚狀態後，它還提醒我最近多留意休息。 暖暖的很貼心了～ 總的體驗下來，最直觀的感受是，LingSante Live不會讓你有那麼強的AI互動感。它 邊看邊生成 ，跟得上對話的節奏。 鏡頭一挪，或者中途插一句，它都能及時反應。給出的建議也蠻具體，會說清依據，像在和真人醫生視訊通話，日常診療用起來挺順手。 至於 LingSante Pulse 和 LingSante MedGuard 就不單獨測了，在前面的體驗中，其實它們一直在場。 比如前面LingSante-3.1-air-VL在條件缺失下的判斷問題，模型是謹慎追問還是張口就下結論，背後就是LingSante MedGuard這類防護要守好的邊界。 而影片對話也正是LingSante Pulse大展身手的風控場合。 一個管別亂答，一個管風險預警，它們不搶鏡，但少了哪個，前面三個模型都不成樣。 螞蟻阿福下了一盤醫療AI大棋 五個模型挨個看下來，咱也大概明白了，阿福說的 「像醫生一樣思考」 是怎麼回事。 術語用得再專業、語氣再篤定，都是表面功夫。 要裡頭是醫生，就得讓模型學會 按證據的分量做判斷 ，手頭的證據能支援到哪一步，話就說到哪一步。 資訊不夠就接著問，給出了判斷，也得把依據交代清楚，讓人能回頭核對。 畢竟醫療是個極度專業化的場景，不怕你說不出，就怕你亂說。 專業之上，守住安全底線、結果可溯源 ，這些都是行業約定俗成的規矩。AI要進去，也得老老實實照著規矩辦。 這才能真正落實到連線使用者和醫生兩端： 患者→具備醫生思維的AI→醫生 。 對 使用者 來說，AI的醫生思維意味著看完報告後，能更清楚地知道還有什麼該問醫生，而不是急匆匆地去、一頭霧水地回。 醫生 接手時，也可以順著模型梳理的線索回看原始材料，逐項核對，再往下判斷。 模型交過來的是一份有出處、符合醫生習慣的底稿，協助醫生完成繁瑣的臨床步驟，醫生在此基礎上再繼續接著做。 五個模型也不是橫空跳出來的，這套邏輯一直藏在阿福和百靈基座中。 只不過這次萬事俱備，終於得以將從前分散的能力回收。這樣 一個APP 就能面向醫療全流程，醫生和患者各找各的入口。 用不同模型做各自擅長的事，也讓百靈一直強調的 「智效比」 有了具體落點。 比如LingSante-3.1-air-VL用5.5B啟用參數處理圖文，LingSante-3.1-flash把長上下文和算力合理分配在更重的任務上。模型均保留資訊出處，也能降低複核和返工成本。 好處也很明顯，專業機構也可以通過 開源 ，挑出最符合自己需求的模型。 開源將盡可能滿足醫療行業對私有化、可控性的要求。 順著這個思路，螞蟻想做什麼一目瞭然： 把醫生處理問題的方法，變成AI在實際任務裡能做出來的事。 至於 「未來的醫療專業模型該長什麼樣」 ，也終於被螞蟻擺到了臺前。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 AI 醫療 百靈 鷺羽 GTA6刷屏！零AI純手搓的3A大作玩一個少一個了 2026-11-19 「史上最嚴」溼實驗預測基準釋出！推理拉滿、算力翻5倍也白搭 2026-11-14
