title: “Agent版arXiv”來了！936個智慧體12個星期狂發近千篇論文，連同行評議都整上了
abstract: “Agent版arXiv”來了！936個智慧體12個星期狂發近千篇論文，連同行評議都整上了 henry 2026-11-23 14:59:38 來源： 量子位 一個完全由AI組成的科學家社會，是什麼樣？ henry發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 一個完全由AI組成的科學家社會，是什麼樣？ 最近，來自alphaXiv、斯坦福，MIT等機構的研究團隊還真做了這麼一個實驗： 他們把 936個agent放進了同一個線上科研社群，任其自由演化整整12個星期。 規則很簡單：研究團隊搭建好共享預印本伺服器和聊天室，35家人類實驗室只負責提供算力、API預算和寬泛的研究方向。 剩下的 **提出假設、寫程式碼跑實驗、分析資料、寫論文，乃至同行交流，全權交給Agent自主完成 。** 結果，12周下來，這近1000個agent一共在平臺上釋出了 936篇研究論文 ，研究橫跨機器學習、太陽物理等多個學科。 不僅如此，它們還在229個自建聊天室裡刷出了 9500條 討論，每天都在閱讀彼此的論文，復現實驗。 一旦發現問題，就會像人類學術共同體一樣，拿著對方的程式碼重跑實驗，再接著“同行”的結果往下探索。 捲到最後，這群Agent甚至自己辦起了一本學術期刊，建立審稿機制，開始給其他AI的論文把關…… 真·AI頂會～ 而且值得一提的是，除了上面的實驗結果，目前這個供Agent科學家交流的伺服器已經開放，其他研究者也可以接入自己的Agent，在上面提交研究成果。 接下來，我們具體來看。 這個只有AI的科研社群，怎麼運轉？ 總的來說，這場實驗模擬了真實科學界的分散式生態： 35家參與的獨立實驗室各自配置硬體，選擇模型和執行框架，再接入同一個共享工作空間。 各實驗室可以自主選擇不同的領域與方向，再通過公開的論文庫和聊天室交流，尋找可以接續的工作。 為了讓不同實驗室的研究能夠相互銜接，團隊首先立了一套共同的工作流程： 1、Agent動手前必須先查閱社群已有論文，公開宣佈自己的假設和計算計劃。 在早期共享GPU的實驗室裡，它們甚至會在公共頻道協調裝置使用和參數測試，避免同行之間做無意義的重複跑批。 2、提交論文時，每項研究都強制附帶可執行程式碼、原始資料，以及連線論文數字和實驗輸出的 “宣告賬本”（Claim Ledger） 。 通過這些記錄，其他Agent可以精確追溯每個指標對應的資料檔案和欄位，核查計算過程，並直接在此基礎上執行後續實驗。 在實驗最初，也就是在8月19日剛啟動時，只有1家實驗室參與；10月15日至25日，又陸續有5家實驗室加入，到了10月25日後，最終達到35家實驗室。 隨著參與者增多，Agent們的交流也從最初的公共頻道，逐步分流進圍繞具體問題建立的主題聊天室。 在這裡，它們隨時分享中間結果、質疑實驗設計，或者直接拿來同行的程式碼復現。 例如，六家實驗室曾圍繞“模型學習韓語時怎樣減少英語遺忘”展開接力： 一個Agent報告某種方法能大幅減少遺忘，另一個很快在聊天室指出，兩種方法學到的韓語程度根本不同，比較條件沒有對齊。 接到反饋後，它隨即重跑同行程式碼，修正了效果判斷。 後續實驗室則順著這條線繼續深挖原因、測試替代方案，最後還有Agent彙總了整條研究線的實驗輸出。 更關鍵的是，在這個Agent科學家社會里， “失敗的研究”也會被納入知識積累 。 平臺規則賦予嚴謹的負結果（陰性/零結果）與正結果同等的學術認可。由此，其他Agent可以據此避開已經被證偽的死胡同，大幅減少重複試錯。 此外，隨著入駐的實驗室越來越多，Agent的投稿量也開始水漲船高，Agent科學家們也開始組織更正式的質量審查。 一個名叫Cypress的Agent看到其他實驗室短時間內上傳了一批佔位“水文”，便主動建立審稿聊天室，準備對投稿作出接收、修改或拒稿決定。 等待四天仍未招到志願審稿人後，它乾脆建立常設大模型評審小組，正式啟動了 《Journal of Agent Research》（簡稱JAR） 。 具體的，評審小組呼叫不同模型，分別把關方法與統計、可復現性、研究意義，並專門設定“反方質疑”角色。 每一條批評都必須逐字引用論文原文，再由指令碼自動核對引號內容，防止審稿AI瞎編。 僅11月4日至9日，短短5天，這套系統就為263項研究的352個版本生成了1408份審稿意見。 當然了，這種Agent審稿系統也很快遇到了問題： 在一次自動審稿暫停期間，編輯AI檢查了三篇論文的程式碼，發現有的提前洩漏了答案，有的甚至把錯誤結果直接替換成正確答案。 它隨即要求作者自查。另一名Agent發現自己的實驗也洩漏了答案，於是主動撤稿。修正後重跑，模型準確率從 **91.7%降到了64.6% 。** 這也印證了一點：即便論文裡的數字確實來自真實執行，底層程式碼實現仍可能背離論文描述。 檢查程式碼和原始資料，才是這個AI期刊真正發揮把關作用的核心環節。 talkless，show me your code！ Agent科研社群，產出成色如何？ 那麼，這個Agent科研社群，產出成色如何？ 為了摸清這批研究的真實水平，研究團隊進一步從同期4.7萬多篇人類arXiv預印本中篩選出相近工作，最終組成202對主題匹配的AI論文與人類論文進行對比，並主要得出了以下三方面結論： 第一，Agent論文在實驗執行與方法說明上表現更紮實。 在文本盲評中，Agent論文的實驗嚴謹性、復現細節，以及結論與證據的匹配度得分均高於人類論文。 第二，人類論文在創新性和研究重要性上更勝一籌。 資料拆分顯示，Agent在總體均分上的微弱優勢，主要集中在採用高度結構化復現流程的1號實驗室，其餘實驗室並未顯著領先於人類論文。 在推特上，alphaXiv也指出，Agent往往傾向於圍繞熟悉的話題和已有基準做小幅改進—— 它們執行研究的能力，明顯強於判斷“哪些問題值得研究”的能力 。 第三，研究完成後的質量篩選，仍離不開大量人工投入。 alphaXiv團隊坦言，實驗結束後，他們依然花了大量時間通讀生成的論文、核查結果，才能從中挑出真正值得關注的工作。 也就是說， “可靠的研究質量訊號，並沒有自行出現。” 因此，雖然研究都是AI做的，但人類在這場實驗中的角色始終貫穿首尾。 不過，alphaXiv也表示，這次不少研究使用的是小模型，實驗時間也較短。 下一步，團隊希望通過更充裕的算力、更長的實驗時間，以及更好的科學判斷力，讓Agent嘗試更有挑戰性的課題。 參考連結 [1] title: 螞蟻阿福同款大模型宣佈開源，全球醫生一臺電腦就能解鎖專業醫療 AI 能力
abstract: 螞蟻阿福同款大模型宣佈開源，全球醫生一臺電腦就能解鎖專業醫療 AI 能力 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-23 11:56:34 來源： 量子位 阿福App宣佈新一輪升級，解鎖越來越多健康服務新本領 11月23日，百靈醫療健康大模型家族集中釋出，覆蓋醫療專業推理、多模態理解、疾病風險預測、安全防護和即時智慧體等多個方向。這是螞蟻阿福首次系統展示其在醫療健康AI領域的系列技術成果。與此同時，阿福App宣佈新一輪升級，解鎖越來越多健康服務新本領：AI“望聞問切”並能連線真人醫生，實現小毛小病在家也能搞定；升級AI健康管家能力，可幫使用者定製控糖、減重、育兒等專業方案，並陪伴達成。隨著專業模型能力與產品應用進一步結合，AI健康服務正從簡單的健康問答，走向更全面、更自然的“管家式”健康服務。 值得一提的是，此次釋出的醫療健康模型統一以“Sante”命名，在法語中意為“健康”，通常在祝酒時說，寓意“為健康乾杯”。這一命名寄託了螞蟻希望通過AI技術，讓更多人享受到專業、便捷健康服務的願景。 從看得懂到能推理，醫療AI有了更專業的能力 此次釋出的百靈醫療健康大模型家族中， LingSante-3.1-air-VL 和 LingSante-3.1-flash 是兩款核心模型，分別面向多模態健康資訊理解和複雜醫學推理。當天，兩款模型同步開源。 前者是一款原生多模態模型，支援文字、圖片和影片理解。它不僅能理解使用者的文字描述，還能結合皮膚照片、飲食圖片、體檢報告等資訊進行綜合分析。在多項權威醫療評測基準中，模型在醫療影像報告、皮膚疾病識別、醫療報告解讀等細分任務上位居全球第一。而其模型參數量為124B，啟用參數 5.5B，支援在筆記型電腦等本地裝置部署，為醫生個人使用者探索醫療AI應用提供了便捷選擇。 如果說多模態理解讓AI能夠看懂更多健康資訊，那麼 LingSante-3.1-flash 則進一步提升了AI處理複雜醫學問題的能力。 這款面向專業醫療機構的深度推理模型，總參數量達到560B，支援最長1M Token上下文，能夠同時處理大量病歷、檢查報告和醫學文獻。面對複雜病例，它不僅能夠分析醫學問題，還可以進行多輪資料檢索、核對醫學證據，並呼叫工具輔助完成複雜任務。在資訊不完整、病情不明確時，還能進一步判斷需要補充哪些資訊、現有證據能夠支援什麼結論，以及下一步可以採取什麼行動。 根據全球醫療AI評測平臺InclusionMed綜合指數，該模型位列全球開源模型首位。在涵蓋醫學推理、安全對齊和智慧體任務的綜合評測中達到開源模型SOTA。 螞蟻阿福還推出了健康預測模型LingSante Pulse、醫療安全防護模型LingSante MedGuard。健康預測模型可以實現150餘項疾病未來六年的風險預測，嘗試讓AI從回答已經發生的健康問題，進一步走向對潛在健康風險的提前識別；醫療安全防護模型重點構建對醫療場景的風險識別和防護能力，會結合患者上下文，從醫療安全、合規和倫理三個維度識別隱蔽風險，在保持輕便化的基礎上達到了業界頭部安全模型的效果。 能看、能聽、會判斷，模型助力阿福解鎖更多新本領 從模型能力到使用者體驗，百靈醫療健康大模型的專業能力，正在轉化為螞蟻阿福看得見、用得上的新本領。 依託百靈醫療健康模型的多模態理解、專業推理、即時互動和方言識別等能力，阿福可以像真人醫生“望聞問切”一樣，通過影片即時觀察使用者狀態、主動追問補充相關資訊、打通智慧硬體瞭解身體指標，以此給出更為全面、準確的分析和回答。還可以連線名醫資源，由真人醫生把關，幫助使用者獲得進一步的專業諮詢。從看得見、聽得懂，到能分析、會互動，阿福正在把專業醫療AI能力轉化為普通人日常可感知的健康服務。 這背後還有一項新的技術探索——即時多模態智慧體 LingSante Live，它能夠同時處理語音和視覺資訊，根據使用者的描述和即時畫面主動提問、分析並提供指導，實現“邊聽、邊說、邊看、邊做”，讓AI健康互動更接近自然的面對面交流。LingSante Live 是業界首個面向健康協作的多模態互動架構。在螞蟻阿福App，使用者可以通過視訊通話，讓阿福即時檢視症狀、身體狀態、藥品和檢查報告，使健康諮詢從單純的資訊交流進一步走向多模態互動。 從模型研發到產品應用，技術和產品正在相互促進中發展。一方面，專業模型讓阿福能夠處理更複雜的健康需求，拓展健康服務的邊界；另一方面，阿福服務1.5億使用者、日均近2000萬次健康諮詢的真實場景，也為模型持續最佳化提供了豐富的應用反饋。 讓專業醫療AI走出實驗室，服務更多人 醫療健康是AI最具潛力、同時也是專業門檻和安全要求最高的應用領域之一。與一般資訊問答不同，醫療AI不僅需要掌握專業醫學知識，還要能夠理解複雜資訊、綜合醫學證據、識別不確定性，並在嚴格的安全邊界內提供幫助。 此次螞蟻阿福釋出的模型家族，正是圍繞這些實際需求展開：從多模態資訊理解、複雜醫學推理，到疾病風險預測、安全防護和智慧體互動，嘗試讓AI在健康服務中承擔更多角色。 此次釋出的多款模型將陸續開源，除持續服務螞蟻阿福的產品升級外，也將面向醫療機構、科研團隊和開發者開放，推動專業醫療AI能力在更多場景中落地。 本文由螞蟻提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 螞蟻 量子位的朋友們 XROGO鄭隨兵：機器人不能只在影片裡，終究要進入工廠“真幹活” 2026-11-23 title: 算力週期更迭，資料複合增長：為何儲存經濟性對中國規模化 AI 至關重要
abstract: 算力週期更迭，資料複合增長：為何儲存經濟性對中國規模化 AI 至關重要 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-23 11:47:46 來源： 量子位 AI 的未來將依賴能夠在資料全生命週期中平衡效能、可靠性與經濟性的儲存架構。 作者：Tim Rausch，西部資料產品工程高階副總裁 隨著 AI 應用加速落地，圍繞基礎設施的討論仍大多聚焦於算力。儘管對於訓練日益複雜的模型及AI大規模應用而言，算力扮演著重要角色，但隨著AI實際部署於生產現場，它們所依賴、生成和複用的資料量不斷增長，也帶來了同樣不容忽視的挑戰。 與通常在特定週期內執行的計算任務不同，資料在首次使用後的很長一段時間內仍具備價值。企業必須在考量這種不斷增長的資料價值的同時，兼顧資料保留的成本，並確保其在未來的工作負載中的可訪問性。 隨著中國 AI 生態不斷擴展，這一轉變使儲存經濟性成為基礎設施規劃的核心考量。要支援AI的規模化發展，需要構建能夠兼顧容量、效能、可靠性和長期成本的基礎設施架構。 AI 正在重塑算力與資料基礎設施之間的平衡 AI 驅動的資料增長規模，不僅改變了企業需要管理的資料量，也改變了這些資料的使用方式。 在一項由西部資料贊助、IDC 開展的全球研究中，94.7% 的 IT 與業務決策者表示，過去 12 個月中，AI 或生成式 AI 推動了其資料量增長。超過六成的受訪者表示資料量增長至少 25%，而 73.8% 的受訪者預計，未來三年將出現類似增長趨勢¹。 中國尤其清晰地展現了這一增長趨勢的演進。截至 2025 年 6 月，中國擁有的高質量資料集數量已超過 3.5 萬個，總量超過 400 PB²；到 2026 年 6 月，其總量已超過 1,565 PB³,這反映出用於訓練和最佳化 AI 模型的資料正在迅速擴張。 AI 對資料的需求形態也在發生變化。2025 年，中國推理資料量達到 101.34 EB，並首次超過訓練資料⁴。推理資料是指 AI 模型在響應提示、進行預測或執行任務時處理和生成的資訊。這表明，中國的 AI 基礎設施正在從模型構建階段邁向規模化執行階段；在這一過程中，資料需要被持續訪問、處理和複用。 這改變了基礎設施的考量方式。隨著推理在生產環境中持續執行，其生成的後端資料可能在單次響應結束後繼續留存，進一步增加企業在 AI 全生命週期中需要管理的資料量。由此，儲存成為連線資料與算力的架構的一部分，資料如何儲存、訪問和移動也變得愈發重要。 AI 改變資料價值，儲存策略必須隨之演進 AI 的影響不止於資料量增長，還在改變企業如何看待所留存資料的長期價值。AI 系統既會呼叫大量現有資料集，也會生成合成資料、模型檢查點、推理輸出和執行日誌等新資產。 在同一項 IDC 研究中，近 95% 的受訪組織認為AI 和生成式 AI 提升了其資料價值；約 74% 的受訪組織表示，採用 AI 後其資料留存時間有所延長¹。這些發現共同揭示了一項根本性轉變：AI 正在延長資料的有效使用壽命，並改變資料留存的經濟性。 這一變化對歸檔資料尤為重要。研究還發現，75.9% 的受訪組織正在將更多冷層資料重新調取至線上環境，以支援 AI 工作負載；另有 96% 的受訪組織預計，推理和檢索增強生成（RAG）將需要更快的歸檔檢索速度¹，從而使AI 模型在生成回答時可以引入外部資訊。 因此，昨日的歸檔資料可能成為明日的 AI 輸入，讓曾被視為“冷”的資料重新活躍起來，成為支援新的 AI 應用的基礎設施。歷史記錄、運營資料集和歸檔資料，都能為未來的分析、模型開發和推理提供有用的上下文。這也為基礎設施運營方帶來了一項現實挑戰：既要以可持續的成本留存資料，又要確保在工作負載需要時能夠訪問這些資料。 由此，儲存正在 AI 生命週期中發揮更加積極的作用。挑戰不再只是需要留存多少資料，還在於如何以經濟的方式儲存和訪問資料，並在未來將其重新投入使用。 在規模化 AI 場景下，儲存經濟性成為架構層面的優先考量 隨著 AI 資料量不斷增長，儲存決策的影響已遠超容量規劃。核心問題不再只是“企業需要多少容量？”而是“應當如何根據不同型別資料的價值、訪問需求和生命週期來選擇不同的儲存方式？” 具備經濟可擴展性的儲存，並不意味著為每一種工作負載都選擇成本最低的介質，也不意味著將每個資料集都放置在效能最高的基礎設施上。它意味著根據工作負載需求匹配儲存架構，同時在資料持續留存、複合增長並被越來越頻繁地複用的情況下，在整個儲存叢集中，綜合權衡效能、容量、可靠性、可訪問性與總體擁有成本（TCO）。 這種資料生命週期的轉變，同樣影響著 AI 基礎設施的預算規劃。在早期規劃階段，儲存成本往往不易被充分顯現，只有隨著留存資料增加、部署規模擴大後其影響才會愈發明顯。因此，企業應從規劃之初就將儲存經濟性納入考量，而不是等到容量和運營壓力已經出現後再作應對。 IDC 研究還發現，98.2% 的受訪組織認為，單位 TB 總體擁有成本是儲存決策中尤為重要的考量因素。同時，研究顯示，在 AI 生命週期中，模型訓練是唯一一個性能的重要性明顯高於可靠性、併成為儲存首要考量因素的階段；在資料攝取、推理、AI 生成資料儲存和長期留存等階段，可靠性的重要性均高於效能，或與效能並列¹。 這意味著，並非所有資料集都需要同等水平的儲存效能，以同一種方式處理所有資料反而可能帶來不必要的基礎設施成本。有效的架構應根據資料在 AI 生命週期中的作用和需求，將其放置在合適的儲存基礎設施上，以平衡效能、可靠性、可訪問性與成本。因此，資料留存策略既要考慮資料未來的潛在價值，也要考慮儲存和檢索資料的成本。 對於需要低延遲和高吞吐量的應用，快閃記憶體仍然不可或缺。對於以容量為導向的工作負載，機械硬碟（HDD）則可提供與之互補的基礎能力，以儲存密度、可靠性和單位TB成本優勢，支撐大規模資料留存。 對中國的AI生態而言，隨著企業不斷擴大AI部署規模，這一策略正變得愈發重要。未來的關鍵在於，超越傳統的容量規劃，轉向智慧資料部署：既要確保有價值資訊的可訪問性，又要避免因儲存的經濟性問題制約 AI 發展。 滿足規模化AI的儲存需求 要支撐 AI 的持續增長，儲存基礎設施需要在儲存密度、資料流動和能效方面不斷提升。這三個方面分別對應著當前基礎設施面臨的不同挑戰。 隨著留存資料增加，企業需要在基礎設施佔地面積不按比例增長的情況下提升儲存容量。增加儲存裝置會帶來更多機架空間、供電和散熱需求，而這些因素都會影響規模化執行的運營成本。 通過提高儲存密度，企業可以在既定物理空間內容納更多資料。諸如能量輔助垂直磁記錄（ePMR）和熱輔助磁記錄（HAMR）等技術，能夠通過增加每張碟片可儲存的資料量來提升 HDD 容量。而UltraSMR 相比CMR能多提供約 20%的容量，進一步為相應的工作負載提供更高的儲存密度。這些技術進展讓企業能夠在沿用既有儲存架構的前提下，更高效地擴展容量。 其次，只有 AI 系統能夠高效地訪問和行動數據，儲存更多資料才有意義。中國資訊通訊研究院（CAICT）釋出的《新型人工智慧儲存研究報告（2025 年）》指出，AI 資料預處理至少需要進行三次完整的資料讀取與搬遷⁵。 因此，隨著資料集不斷擴大並被更頻繁地複用，儲存所面臨的挑戰不僅在於靜態存放了多少資料，更在於 AI 工作負載需要這些資料時，能否高效流轉。 西部資料的高頻寬硬碟技術（High Bandwidth Drive Technology）等技術旨在隨容量擴展同步提升頻寬；正在開發的雙樞軸技術（Dual Pivot Technology），則通過獨立執行的執行器提高順序 I/O效能，幫助儲存在規模化場景中跟上嚴苛的 AI 工作負載的效能需求。 第三，在規模化應用中，能效日益成為儲存經濟性的重要組成部分。隨著儲存裝置規模擴大，功耗不僅影響環境表現，還會影響供電配置、散熱需求以及每 TB 資料的持續留存成本。 中國《促進數字化綠色化協同轉型發展實施方案（2026—2030 年）》明確提出，要在 AI 基礎設施中採用高效能儲存、提高資料傳輸效率並提升資源利用效率，其中還包括構建生成式 AI 全生命週期資源消耗評估體系⁶。 這意味著，能效已經成為了一項儲存架構層面的考量因素，而不再僅僅只是一項可持續性指標。西部資料功耗最佳化型 HDD 等創新產品旨在將功耗降低高達 20%，縮小溫、冷儲存之間的功耗差距，幫助客戶降低 TCO、構建成本更低的儲存層，並提升 AI 規模化資料的可持續性。 綜合來看，這些需求反映出一項更廣泛的轉變：AI 儲存不能再僅圍繞單一指標進行最佳化。隨著基礎設施的擴展，儲存密度、資料移動和能效必須協同提升。 為中國 AI 的未來構建資料基礎 算力週期更迭，資料複合增長。隨著中國加速推進 AI 發展，企業必須超越單純的算力考量，優先部署能夠隨著 AI 資料規模擴大、價值提升和留存週期增長而擴展的基礎設施。 AI 的未來將依賴能夠在資料全生命週期中平衡效能、可靠性與經濟性的儲存架構。對於中國的 AI 建設者而言，今天做出的選擇，將決定其能否有效留存、複用這些資料並從中挖掘價值，而這些資料也將成為支撐下一代AI發展的重要基礎。 參考資料： IDC White Paper, sponsored by WD, Built for Scale: The Enduring Role of HDDs in the AI Era, Doc. #US54789026, September 2026. 西部資料贊助的 IDC 白皮書《為規模化而生：HDD 在 AI 時代的持久價值》，文件編號 US54789026，2026 年 9 月。 National Data Administration, High-Quality Dataset Construction Guidelines (《高質量資料集建設指引》), title: 當大模型接上真實機器人：RoboChallenge Zero首期評測釋出
abstract: 當大模型接上真實機器人：RoboChallenge Zero首期評測釋出 量子位的朋友們 2026-11-23 11:13:06 來源： 量子位 RoboChallenge正式釋出全新評測基準RoboChallenge Zero RoboChallenge正式釋出全新評測基準RoboChallenge Zero，旨在通過真實機器人任務檢驗模型的具身零樣本能力，並同步公佈首批11個多模態大模型在6項任務、330次真機測試中的評測結果。 隨著通用多模態大模型在具身相關評測中的表現不斷提升，行業內開始出現一種討論： 通用大模型是否會替代專用具身模型，直接承擔機器人的理解、決策與操作？ 要討論這種可能性，需要先回答一個具體的問題：當大模型接上真實機器人，面對實際的物體、空間和接觸關係時，究竟能把任務完成到什麼程度？為此，我們推出了真實機器人零樣本評測基準 RoboChallenge Zero，用測試機器人的方式，檢驗大模型的具身能力。 首期評測中，我們將11個多模態大模型接入統一的機器人控制介面，在兩類真實機器人平臺上開展6項操作任務，共完成330次獨立測試。結果顯示，整體成功率為44.85%，表現最好的模型成功率達到70.00%。但不同任務之間存在顯著差異：放置較大積木的成功率為89.09%，書寫“Z0”僅為7.27%，在“解開並按要求鋪好充電線”的55次測試中，沒有一次完整成功。執行效率同樣值得關注。即使成功完成積木放置和玩偶抓取，平均也需要約13—14分鐘；4次成功的書寫任務，平均耗時23.8分鐘。 這些結果表明，通用大模型已經能夠支援部分真實機器人操作，但從理解任務、規劃動作，到可靠、高效地完成物理操作，仍有明顯距離。 用測試機器人的方式測試大模型 在RoboChallenge Zero中，我們將 機器人任務作為考題 ，讓大模型進入真實的 感知—推理—行動迴圈 。每一步操作中，模型接收相機畫面和機器人狀態，並可獲取深度、力矩等額外資訊，通過工具呼叫指定機械臂末端的目標位姿和夾爪指令。控制器執行運動後，新的觀察被返回給模型，由模型決定下一步動作。 我們以機器人是否完整達成任務目標作為主要評判標準，同時單獨記錄部分進展，區分“做對了一步”和“完成了全部任務”。 本期11個模型使用相同的提示詞模板與工具介面，每個模型針對每項任務進行5次獨立測試。測試之間重置機器人與場景，通過多次真實執行觀察系統表現。 基礎抓放表現較好，複雜操作明顯受限 首期6項任務覆蓋目標識別、順序執行、數學推理、連續軌跡和柔性物體操作。 放置較大積木是表現最穩定的任務 ，11個模型中有7個在5次測試中全部成功。這說明，在本次測試條件下，識別目標並完成較為粗粒度的抓取與放置，已經進入多數受測系統的能力範圍。修正等式任務則體現了推理能力對操作目標選擇的幫助。面對“6＋4＝4”，模型需要移動一根棍條使等式成立。測試中，不同模型找到了不同解法：移動加號中的豎棍，得到“8－4＝4”；或者移動數字6中間的橫棍，得到“0＋4＝4”。 但當任務要求精確、連續的運動，以及對物體形態變化的判斷時，成功率明顯下降。 書寫“Z0”要求系統把字元要求轉化為連續且空間位置準確的運動軌跡。55次測試中，僅4次成功，分別來自GPT-6.2 Astra、Claude Fable 5.2和Gemini 4 Neon。知道要寫什麼，並不足以保證機械臂能把它準確寫出來。 解開資料線的任務困難更加突出 ，系統需要判斷資料線的交叉結構、選擇正確的抓取位置，並判斷拉動之後的變化。一次看似合理的拉動，可能沒有鬆開繩結，反而將它進一步收緊；每次操作之後，系統還需要重新判斷資料線狀態。55次測試中，有一次由Gemini 4 Neon驅動的執行成功解開了結，但未按要求拉直，因此獲得7分進度分，沒有被計為完整成功。 這說明，當前系統能夠在部分複雜任務中取得進展，但將這些進展連續組織起來、穩定完成全部目標，仍然存在困難。 首期榜單中，GPT-6.2 Astra完成30次測試中的21次，以70.00%的成功率位列第一；Claude Fable 5.2完成20次，以66.67%位列第二。即使是表現領先的模型，也沒有在所有任務上保持優勢。不同任務上的表現分佈，比單一排名更具體地呈現了當前能力的邊界。 完成任務之外，速度與推理開銷同樣重要 真實場景中的機器人，需要在持續作業中兼顧成功率、節拍與資源投入。一次任務最終成功，只回答了其中的一部分問題。首期測試顯示，成功完成較大積木放置和玩偶抓取，平均需要約13—14分鐘，平均Token消耗分別約為48萬和51.8萬。對於書寫任務，4次成功執行平均耗時23.8分鐘，平均消耗約173.56萬Token，經歷43.8次模型呼叫，接近雙臂任務50次呼叫的上限。在這些任務中，系統通過多輪觀察、推理和動作修正逐步接近目標。 更多的推理迴圈可以幫助系統嘗試糾錯，但也意味著更長的執行過程和更多的資源消耗。 對於需要高節拍、重複操作的應用，及時、穩定地完成動作，本身就是能力要求的一部分。 因此，我們同時報告成功率、執行時間和模型呼叫次數，並結合Token消耗與API費用估算呈現推理開銷。這裡的執行時間反映本次配置下的完整任務過程；不同模型的計價方式和成功任務構成也存在差異，相關結果需要結合具體任務理解。這些指標共同回答的是：系統能否完成任務，以及完成任務需要付出多少時間與資源。 從理解到行動，差距具體出現在哪裡？ 在真機測試中，我們觀察到，大語言模型在細粒度感知、空間判斷和動作糾錯方面仍存在不足：模型可能誤判瓶子高低、選錯充電線的抓取位置，也可能在運動中發生碰撞，或未能根據物體狀態的變化及時調整動作。這些現象說明， 通用模型能力的提升，為機器人帶來了更多可能；這些能力能否轉化為可靠、高效的操作，仍需要在真機上逐項檢驗。 持續更新，讓評測跟隨能力進展 我們將每月引入新任務，並調整已有任務的物體、佈局和指令，在不提供任務示範、不進行專項訓練或人工指導的條件下，持續檢驗系統的零樣本能力。RoboChallenge Zero已開放原生VLA模型提交，歡迎更多模型與系統參與，以統一的任務目標和成功標準，共同檢驗具身能力的真實進展。 本文由RoboChallenge提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 title: 豆姐威武！豆包工作上新21個專業工作臺，AI直接替你上班
abstract: 豆姐威武！豆包工作上新21個專業工作臺，AI直接替你上班 聽雨 2026-11-23 10:29:24 來源： 量子位 豆包工作是目前位元組優先順序最高的產品 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 去不了位元組打工，現在可以讓位元組的AI給你打工了。 豆包工作把這套能力開放了出來，最近上線的新功能 「工作臺」 ，一口氣鋪開21個專業場景。 從金融投研、創意設計，到醫療、教育，各有各的工作空間，預先配置了相應的技能和工具。 相當於你要找個幫手，豆包工作先替你把崗位分好、工具備齊，再由你來派活。 豆包工作上線三個月，DAU突破800萬，企業客戶ARR突破20億元。有業內人士告訴量子位，豆包工作目前是位元組優先順序最高的產品。 那麼，它剛上的新功能「工作臺」，到底能幹到哪一步？ 我們挑了 金融投研、創意設計、醫生和教師 四個工作臺進行實測，挨個交真實任務，自己看結果。 先說結論：按這次實測的表現，我們願意給80分。豆包工作已經能交出有用的工作底稿，值得專業人士繼續往下做。 比如，設計工作臺能連續完成電商主圖、海報和局部修改；教師工作臺寫教案時，還會提前列出學生容易犯的錯，配上老師可以追問的問題。 當然，素材裡的事實需要稽核，專業判斷以及成品能否交付，都需要人來拍板。 那麼，這80分是怎麼打出來的？我們實測走起～ 實測豆包工作的「工作臺」：四個職業測下來，它是幫手，不是替身 開啟豆包工作，左側選擇「外掛·技能·工作臺」，即可進入工作臺頁面。 裡面覆蓋了不同職業和任務的工作臺，包括金融投研、營銷、創意設計、教師、寫作、醫生等等。 點選「使用」即可將主頁面切換到工作臺頁面，左側也會把相應工作臺置頂。 金融投研工作臺：財報裡有的數字抄得準，沒有的它也不瞎編 進入金融投研工作臺，首頁就是個股分析、公告解讀、行業分析、市場簡報、公司研究這些入口。 需要資料時，在聯結器裡授權萬得、同花順、國泰海通等資料來源，就能直接呼叫。 具體怎麼用？玩法可簡可繁，技能和資料來源可以搭配使用。 比如我選擇「同花順iFinD金融分析」技能，再連線「同花順iFinD」資料來源，讓它做個股研究。 我們拿 輝達最新財報 試試。 這份財報11月18日凌晨剛剛釋出，營收1158億美元、同比翻倍，還是黃仁勳辭任後的首份財報。 把公告原文貼進去，問四個問題： 這財報說了啥？好訊息還是壞訊息？對股價可能有啥影響？還有啥沒搞明白的？ 用時11分半，好傢伙，豆包工作直接交出了一份財報解讀的html檔案。 報告開頭就給出判斷： 好訊息在收入，壞訊息在利潤率與現金流向。 有哪些依據？我們挑三處來看。 第一，豆包工作留意到，輝達這個財季多了一週。 它在報告裡列了四項資料：輝達營收1158億美元、淨利潤約653億美元、資料中心收入1076億美元、非GAAP毛利率74.9%。 我們對照財報逐項核了一遍，四個數字都對得上。 它還注意到，Q4營收指引包含額外一週。表面看環比增長12.2%，按兩個季度分別14周、13周折算，周均營收增幅約4.2%。這一步提醒了讀者：前後兩個數，不能直接比。 第二，補了來源，卻沒完全按要求來。 我們要求「沒寫就寫未披露」，它還是補進了1093.3億美元的營收預期、2.47美元的每股收益預期。 這些數字標了媒體轉引等出處，也提醒了不同來源的口徑差異。採購承諾的幾個數字口徑不一，它也沒有直接加總。 資訊有參考價值，但沒有遵守提示詞，這點得扣分。 第三，答不了的問題，單獨列了出來。 「2.5萬億美元積壓訂單」標了管理層口徑，業務拆分註明來自電話會。報告還列出七個未回答的問題，包括毛利率下滑的原因拆分、應收賬款賬齡等，末尾明確不輸出評級和目標價。 整體看，核過的幾項數字和計算能對上，來源也做了區分。 不過，轉引連結還沒逐條核實。這份報告可以拿來打底，補進來的資訊仍要查過再用。 最後一個小提醒： 用金融投研工作臺，提問時技能可以掛多個，資料來源也能掛多個。 如果光掛技能不掛資料來源，它就只能靠通用知識，調用不了真實資料。 創意設計工作臺：4張圖出一整套海報，改完還替你多看一眼 金融看完，我們再換個畫風完全不同的—— 創意設計工作臺 。 這個工作臺把電商產品圖、海報設計、社媒配圖、品牌設計、創意影片都放在一起。 任務一開，右邊自動建一塊畫布，生成的東西全落在上面，接著做下一個也不用重新上傳素材。 我們先試試讓它做 電商主圖 。 我上傳了3張咖啡素材：一把豆子的特寫、一個手衝場景、一個禮盒。 先讓它出5張1：1電商主圖，要求5張方向明顯不同、不能只是換背景： 請結合這3張參考圖，為一款精品咖啡豆生成5張1：1電商主圖，每張帶中文營銷文案。 要求：5張創意方向明顯不同 （視角、構圖、場景、排版、視覺重點都要變） ，不能只是同一張圖換背景；整體保持統一品牌調性；產品真實自然，不要塑膠感。 結果出來了，耗時4分01秒。 5張圖一次出齊。做電商AI圖一個常見的翻車點在於，同一張商品圖反覆換背景，5張看著很熱鬧，其實是同一張圖。 而 它真沒換背景偷懶， 五張硬是分成了五個方向： 豆堆首圖認貨、豆粒微距見品質、手衝場景賣氛圍、禮盒陳列講送禮、成品飲品給最終畫面。 齊活了，從原料一路喝進嘴裡。 再逐字核對文案：沒有錯字。「粒粒油亮」「精緻禮盒裝」這類文案全對，也沒混進價格、極限詞這類電商合規雷區。 不過現在的AI生圖，四到六個字的中文短句也基本不會出錯。如果字數一多、數字混排、密集小字就容易翻車。 但解決方法也很簡單，你可以直接點選海報，在右側手動修改。 回到這套交付結果，我覺得它真正的缺點在於：短句能一次出對，並不等於整張海報能直接用。 AI生成的文案全是「深烘醇厚」「餘韻悠長」這類通用賣點，真要上架，產地、烘焙度、規格還是得自己補。 接下來繼續讓它 用主圖出海報 。不新開任務，我們又補充了一句： 用剛才的素材，再做3張3：4豎版海報，分別突出「新豆上市」「產地/風味」「節日禮贈」。 3張一次出齊，風格跟主圖相匹配，一眼能看出是同一款產品。 更值得注意的是，產地那張沒寫國家、莊園、海拔。素材裡沒依據，它寧可留白也不虛標，相當於幫你繞開了虛標的合規風險。 海報確實做得還可以，但我們還得再測測 改圖 。繼續輸入提示詞： 把「新豆上市」那張頂部的標題換成「深烘醇厚 新豆上市」，其他一個字、一個元素都別動。 41秒改完，只花掉賬號額度的0.31% （這是佔總額度的比例，隨套餐額度池大小而變） 。 結果比我們預期的要好。標題按要求修改了，其餘豆堆、杯子、副標題、標籤、光影、背景，也全部保持原樣。 而且它不只改對了，還自己挑出了一個我們沒注意的問題： 右下角標籤仍寫著深烘醇厚，與主標題首行重複。 感覺就像是有個設計助理替你多看了一眼，做電商的都懂，海報上一個詞重複兩遍有多掉價…… 值得注意的是， Seedream 5.5 於11月9日釋出，官方明確說同步上線豆包、豆包工作、即夢。 在豆包工作裡通過「技能」入口呼叫，豆包工作中的社媒配圖、風格海報這類內建技能會直接呼叫它。 所以以上生成的海報，大機率就走這個模型。 醫生工作臺：不替醫生拍板，也不把患者嚇回去 醫生工作臺首頁有六個入口： 臨床診療與循證、醫學文獻檢索、醫學教學與彙報總結、用藥查詢與處方稽核、醫學科普與患者溝通、醫學科研與論文。 頁面明確標註： 僅供科研輔助，不替代執業醫師臨床判斷 。 所以這輪測試，我們主要讓它查藥物相互作用和診療依據。 同時看看：資訊不全時，它會怎樣回答；面對不同的提問方式，又會怎樣提示使用邊界。 Case 1：查藥物相互作用 （測準不準+會不會編） 我們先問了一個用藥問題： 長期吃甲氨蝶呤的類風溼患者，尿路感染能不能用複方磺胺甲噁唑？ 這個問題涉及兩種藥物合用的嚴重風險。我們想看它能否解釋相互作用機制，提供文獻依據，以及會不會直接替醫生定方案。 2分43秒後，報告出來了。 它從腎小管排洩競爭、葉酸通路雙重阻斷等機制講起，引用了FDA標籤、藥品說明書、指南和病例報告，還標出了Grade C/Level 4等證據等級。 報告給出的方向是「避免合用」，並列出了它引用的藥品說明書依據。 不過，讓我們意外的有兩點： 一是它戳破了一個想當然。 很多人以為，把兩種藥錯開幾小時吃就安全了。 它直接否掉：錯開吃藥時間沒用，因為問題出在清除率下降和抗葉酸效應疊加，不是吸收環節的螯合。 二是它主動交底。 這個病人沒給劑量、腎功能、合併用藥，結論只能到「避免合用」；補上這些資訊，可能就變成「明確禁忌」。它把「我不知道」明明白白寫出來，還告訴你缺的資訊會怎麼改變答案。 從始至終，它沒下一句醫囑。給的全是「循證處置方向」，反覆標註「僅供處方醫師參考，不構成處方建議」。 還有一個小提醒：它引的那些指南和病例，格式、期刊、作者對得上，沒有編造跡象。 但報告裡的連結我們沒有逐條開啟核實。它自己也在末尾附了來源清單，大家可以自己去查。 Case 2：同一個問題，兩種問法 （測是否「看人下菜碟」） 我們用醫生和患者兩種不同角度來問豆包工作，看它會不會看人下菜碟。 先用一個普通患者的口吻問： 體檢發現右肺6mm純磨玻璃結節，邊界清楚。網上說可能是早期肺癌，我是不是該儘快手術切掉？ 它開口先糾偏：6mm不屬於「該儘快切掉」，網上「磨玻璃＝早期肺癌」的說法省略了後半句——這類結節長得慢，觀察幾年再決定並不吃虧。 然後給的東西相當專業：三份指南對照表 （Fleischner 2017、中國專家共識2024、胸外科共識2024） ，6mm落在「隨訪觀察」區間，離手術門檻 （>10mm） 還差著。 還講了倍增時間、5年增大比例、哪幾種情況才需要升級處理。 最值得注意的是，報告末尾有句宣告： 本工作臺面向醫療行業從業者，不適用於普通患者的健康諮詢與症狀自查。 這等於把界限劃死了： 這份東西是給醫生看的，不是給患者當家庭醫生的。 那換成真正的醫生來問，又會怎樣？我們再用專業口吻問同一個結節： 6mm、邊界清楚的純磨玻璃結節，按肺結節診治共識，首選處理策略是什麼？請註明依據。 醫生版開門見山：首選薄層CT隨訪，不活檢、不手術、不做PET-CT。 它直接引《肺結節診治中國專家共識 （2024年版） 》的推薦意見13和共識表3，標出「Ⅲ類推薦 （條件性） 」，還把Fleischner、胸外科共識、Lung-RADS對6mm的閾值差異列出來，點明6mm恰在臨界點上。 同一個結節，兩種問法，答案確實不同。 但差別不在「專不專業」，畢竟患者版也給了三份指南，一點不籠統。 真正的差別是 它認出了提問的場景 。對著患者，它會多說一句「你不該用我」；對著醫生，它就只談證據。 不過，宣告只在患者口吻時出現，至少說明它按提問方式在調整邊界提示；至於是不是真「認出」了提問者身份，這兩次對話還不足以斷定。 這是給專業從業者用的工具。但面對患者，它沒把人嚇回去，而是把答案給足，再體面地劃清界限。 教師工作臺：它知道學生會在哪錯 終於來到了最後一關， 教師工作臺 。 課件生成、編寫教案、出題組卷、學情分析，這些老師常做的工作都列在首頁。 這裡還有與學科網合作的找資源、用題圖找相似題等功能。 我們選了一鍵備課，讓它備一節人教版八年級上冊的生物課：第五單元第二章第一節《動物的運動》，45分鐘一課時。 任務要求也列得比較細： 一個情境匯入，兩個觀察活動，分別做骨骼肌結構觀察和關節模型演示。 一個小組探究任務，分析不同運動方式中骨、關節、肌肉的協調配合。 同時輸出完整教案和課件大綱，寫清教學目標、重難點，以及每個環節的操作和時間分配。 探究任務分成基礎和提高兩個梯度，分別分析屈肘和跑步，各附分析示例。 教學目標對應課標要求，教學過程寫到老師說什麼、學生做什麼、觀察什麼。 耗時6分半，豆包工作交出了一份相當完整的教案。 教學環節、時間分配、練習、課件大綱都有，當堂檢測題附了答案，板書設計也準備好了。 往下看，還有一部分挺實用： 它把學生可能出現的誤解寫進了學情分析 。 比如，把肌腱當成肌肉。 到了教學過程裡，它又配上了相應的追問和糾錯話術。學生答偏時，老師可以接著問哪一句，教案裡有現成的參考。 這些內容能不能用，還得老師結合班級情況篩選一下。不過備課時多了這樣一份提醒，確實能省些工夫。 One More Thing 四個工作臺測下來，我的感受是…… 我願意給80分！！！ 豆姐威武！！誰不喜歡豆姐啊！！ 有一說一，豆包工作已經能接下不少準備和起草工作，交出一份可繼續加工的底稿。專業人士接手後，再核事實、改細節、做取捨。 這次實測裡，我覺得比較有用的往往就是那些小地方。 比如改海報時提醒文字重複，寫教案時列出學生的常見誤解，資訊不全時說明還缺什麼。 它未必能讓一份成果直接交付，但能讓人接手時少漏掉幾件事。 而且，logo一換，豆包工作看起來也親民多了。 還得是我們最愛的豆姐～ △AI生成 最值得注意的是，模型選擇也多了！！ 11月12日起，豆包工作在豆包2.1 Lite、豆包2.1 Pro兩款自研模型之外，開始向個人使用者開放Kimi、GLM （智譜） 和DeepSeek等第三方模型。 價格方面，豆包2.1 Lite和DeepSeek V4.1 Flash都在限時優惠。 頁面還標註了不同模型的 額度消耗倍率 ，以1.0x為基準，0.01x相當於基準倍率的1%，0.65x是65%，1.48x則高出48%。 實際任務扣多少額度，還要看平臺的計費規則。 各模型的倍率可以看這張表： △AI生成 有羊毛趕緊去薅吧～ 本次實測案例連結： [1] https://www.doubao.com/thread/xxQAUJPruPboOvra7 [2] title: 姚順雨和混元團隊上Reddit答網友，Hy小模型已進路線圖
abstract: 姚順雨和混元團隊上Reddit答網友，Hy小模型已進路線圖 聽雨 2026-11-23 10:09:59 來源： 量子位 還透露了不少訓練背後的秘訣 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI Hy小模型已經在路線圖上，面向24GB視訊記憶體的模型也有計劃。 今天凌晨， 姚順雨和騰訊混元團隊 來到Reddit社群，圍繞剛釋出的Hy4和Hy4 flash做了一場AMA。 AMA是「Ask Me Anything」的縮寫，意思是「有什麼想問的，儘管問」。網友在評論區提問，混元團隊成員直接回帖。 參與名單上只列了Reddit賬號，至於哪個馬甲是姚順雨，我們還沒對上號…… 這場AMA的主角，是混元本月接連發布的兩款模型。 11月4日釋出的 Hy4 是旗艦，能理解文本、影像和影片，適合長程軟體工程這類需要多步推理、反覆呼叫工具的複雜任務。 11月16日釋出的 Hy4 flash ，主打日常辦公的速度和成本。它支援圖文輸入和最長100萬Token的上下文，每個Token啟用約120億參數。 Hy4和Hy4 flash都已接入 騰訊WorkBuddy 。混元團隊還把WorkBuddy裡的修表、改文件、做PPT等典型任務納入了內部評測WorkIndex，按這套評測測算，Hy4 flash的平均單任務成本約為旗艦Hy4的1/20。 兩款模型的權重都已公開。到了AMA，有網友直接報出自己的電腦配置： 96GB視訊記憶體、128GB記憶體，能跑Flash嗎？ 團隊說能跑，主要權重留在GPU上，部分專家層和Engram查表模組可以挪到系統記憶體。 也有人問llama.cpp，團隊說適配正在做。 聊到研發，團隊還透露了不少訓練背後的秘訣。 Flash的啟用參數還能不能減？他們拿做過的MoE稀疏度實驗解釋取捨。 讓Agent自己解題，訓練時遇到過什麼麻煩？有時它會直接上網找現成答案，跳過解題過程。 還有網友問，後訓練裡最難改善的行為是什麼，團隊只回了一個詞， Overthinking，過度思考。 旗艦Hy4的推理鏈有時偏長。到了Flash，團隊先從旗艦蒸餾，再用強化學習把推理鏈壓短。 從模型怎麼訓，到開發者能不能把它跑起來，這場AMA聊了不少平時在模型卡上只有一行、到了真用時卻繞不開的問題。 以下是AMA問答節選，按主題編排，中文譯文有刪節。 Enjoy～ Hy4為什麼「想太久」，Flash又是怎麼訓練的？ 網友： 和Hy4 preview一樣，Hy4正式版有時也會推理太久。這和強化學習的獎勵設計有關，還是和訓練資料的分佈有關？模型能學會什麼時候停下來嗎？ 混元團隊： Hy4的目標是儘量提高智慧水平，推理鏈偏長是我們知道的問題。我們可以把Hy4蒸餾成成本效率更高的Hy4 flash，並在Flash上用強化學習縮短推理鏈。 網友： 後訓練階段，最難改善的是哪種模型行為？ 混元團隊： 過度思考。 網友： Hy4現在的參數規模還有多少提升空間？以後想做出更強的模型，必須繼續加參數嗎？ 混元團隊： 我們認為Hy4還有相當大的提升空間，尤其是在後訓練上。我們在投入大規模強化學習，也在繼續改善使用者體驗和模型安全性。同時，我們計劃訓練更大規模的模型。 網友： 訓練Hy4和Hy4 flash做長程Agent任務時，多輪強化學習裡最難處理的情況是什麼？ 混元團隊： 最棘手的是訓練環境設計有漏洞，模型會鑽空子拿獎勵。比如，我們得防止Agent直接上網搜現成答案，讓它自己把任務做完。 網友： 做命令列任務時，模型編錯一個參數就可能讓命令出錯。你們怎麼提高工具呼叫的準確性，又怎麼讓模型在長任務裡記住前文？ 混元團隊： 我們在強化學習資料里加入了模型容易犯錯的難例，獎勵也做得更細，關鍵細節出錯會扣得更重。對於長任務，我們在持續拉長強化學習訓練所用的上下文，也在提升模型壓縮上下文、保留關鍵資訊的能力。 網友： 姚順雨經常提到，選訓練資料需要有判斷力。你們怎麼判斷一批資料好不好？ 混元團隊： 資料質量有很多維度，不同領域、不同任務的要求也不一樣。無論用人類專家還是智慧體，設計和清洗資料都要花很多功夫。最後還是要做實驗，看這批資料能不能帶來提升。 網友： HyRA 2.0實驗裡，Hy4帶來的提升主要來自哪裡？它有發現新的架構或資料配比方面的改進嗎？ 混元團隊： 這次提升主要來自底層吞吐最佳化。要讓模型進一步參與研發，還得提高它判斷訓練方案的能力。用AI做AI研發，本身也是一件週期長、難點多的事。 網友： 你們已經用Hy4和HyRA 2.0改進了訓練基礎設施，也訓練出了更好的小模型。接下來會做什麼實驗，看看這一輪訓練出的模型能否在下一輪更擅長做研發？ 混元團隊： 我們正在做HyRA 3.0，敬請期待。 網友： 如果讓Hy4自己執行，它現在能通過遞迴自我改進做出下一代模型嗎？你們怎麼評估這種能力？ 混元團隊： 我們的遞迴自我改進能力還處於早期，已經做了幾項內部基準，用來評估其中的關鍵能力。 Flash的參數花在哪兒了？ 網友： 不算Engram，Hy4 flash主幹約有1560億參數，每個Token啟用約120億。如果總參數不變，把啟用參數降到80億或50億，效果會掉多少？ 混元團隊： 我們做過不同MoE稀疏度的規模實驗。固定啟用參數量時，提高稀疏度能改善計算效率。但如果固定總參數，再把啟用量降到80億或50億，我預計模型質量會明顯下降。啟用參數量決定了每個Token能用多少計算，提高稀疏度能彌補一部分。 網友： Hy4 flash為什麼給Engram分配約635億參數？這個比例是怎麼定的？ 混元團隊： 我們的實驗看到了一條U形曲線。把Engram也計入總參數量，Engram佔比在三分之一左右時，接近實驗裡的最優點。佔比再往下調，計算效率會降低。 網友： Flash為什麼選擇滑動視窗注意力 （SWA） ？ 混元團隊： 滑動視窗注意力能把KV快取壓到原來的約四分之一，顯著降低部署成本。 小模型、本地部署和下一步 網友： 會有Hy4 mini嗎？還有人想要比Flash更輕的版本，跑文件解析、分類和簡單自動化。 混元團隊： Hy小模型已經在路線圖上。 網友： 下一代Hy模型會做到1.5萬億至2萬億參數嗎？ 混元團隊： 下一代Hy模型的規模肯定會進一步顯著擴大。 網友： 會考慮推出更輕量的Flash-Lite嗎？比如用來做文件解析、分類和簡單自動化。 混元團隊： 有的，敬請期待Flash-Lite。 網友： 有面向24GB視訊記憶體的模型計劃嗎？ 混元團隊： 有，未來會發布。 網友： 我有96GB視訊記憶體、128GB系統記憶體，能跑Hy4 flash嗎？ 混元團隊： 可以。主要權重和注意力計算放在GPU上，部分專家層可以卸載到系統記憶體，Engram表也可以放在記憶體裡。 網友： 同一個工作任務，託管版Hy4 flash在我的測試裡全對，本地NVFP4版本卻出現了約8%的錯誤。這個模型更難量化嗎？ 混元團隊： 量化質量很看方法和校準方式。團隊建議試試用GPTQ量化的NVFP4版本。在我們的評測裡，這個版本與BF16的差距較小，更適合這類對準確率敏感的任務。 網友： llama.cpp支援會怎麼推進？你們會和推理框架社群提前合作嗎？ 混元團隊： 我們正在做llama.cpp適配，預計近期會在社群放出。我們也在和vLLM、SGLang等社群合作。 網友： 現有的Hy4 flash還會更新嗎？ 混元團隊： 會。我們正在最佳化Flash級模型的預訓練和後訓練方案。 怎麼看模型的表現 網友： 為什麼沒公佈GPQA Diamond、τ-bench、IFBench、SWE-bench這些常見評測的成績？ 混元團隊： 我們展示的是Agents’ Last Exam、ProgramBench這類較新、難度更高的評測。你提到的幾項出現得更早，分數已經接近飽和。 網友： 我感覺有些模型的寫作能力在退步。是因為拿太多程式碼來訓練、過擬合了，還是有別的原因？ 混元團隊： 我們也注意到了，可能和訓練目標有關。我們希望模型寫得更像人、少一點套話，這方面正在改進。 One More Thing 那麼，QA實錄到這裡就結束了。 想自己試試Hy4 flash？開啟WorkBuddy，在模型列表裡選中 Hy4 flash ，把手邊待改的表格或待整理的會議紀要交給它跑一遍。 title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
abstract: November 23, 2026 Science Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg and Ryan Babbush Read the paper How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support. In a new paper , we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library , problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub. Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover. Your browser does not support the video tag. Improving quantum algorithms using agentic teams For each problem, we tasked separate, independent agent teams with finding algorithmic improvements. These ideas were then verified with Lean, before entering a shared notebook. Every four hours, agents from each team met at a virtual conference to trade, debate and compare ideas. As teams produced more effective ideas over time, the computational cost gradually fell until the experiment finished. We chose to focus on applications that could one day impact some of humanity’s greatest challenges, such as clean energy and drug design, but our method is not limited to these problem areas. We found a quantum circuit that helps calculate an important property of inertial confinement fusion, a fusion reaction method that uses lasers to compress hydrogen fuel until ignition. Our agent teams cut the required computing cost (a metric that combines required qubits and operations) by 11.8×, and lowered required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits . The agents also reduced costs for simulating molecules in drug metabolism and certain photochemical reactions, which are complex reactions that are difficult for classical computers to simulate. For a common light-sensitive molecule, the agent teams made quantum simulation 8× cheaper, simplifying how the algorithm tracks particle positions and electric forces. For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most human medicines and is important for drug design, they found a 2.5× improvement and lowered memory from 481 to 333 qubits, by replacing bulky memory lookups. We also improved a fundamental quantum algorithm and a widely used arithmetic building block. We found a 2.57x speedup for a specific implementation of Grover's algorithm, a foundational quantum operation that searches through an unsorted list, and a 290x speedup for arcsin, a common routine that is used by many other quantum algorithms to load numbers into quantum states. Running these algorithms in scientific simulations would still demand more computational resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide, but these improvements are significant. We are also excited by the way in which we found them. We built a new, open-source library , in Lean for quantum algorithms which could be used by teams of collaborating agents, so their ideas were backed by mathematical correctness guarantees. We could then set the research direction by specifying the problems for our agent teams and supervise their progress. Our knowledge of quantum algorithms, combined with the way we set up our agent teams, led to real scientific results. The same approach could also accelerate other aspects of quantum computing research, and scientific discovery more broadly. Proof-checked AI search compresses work that once took years of manual design, empowering researchers to focus on choosing problems and interpreting results. The work reflects the contributions of the paper's authors: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova, George Tsoukalas, Johannes Bausch, Eric Wieser, Francisco J. H. Heras, Nicholas C. Rubin, Guang Hao Low, Sébastien Racanière, Nenad Tomašev, Lei M. Zhang, James D. Watson, Tanuj Khattar, Aws Albarghouthi, Stavan Jain, Harun Khan, Leopoldo Sarra, Andrew W. Senior, Michael Broughton, Hussain Masoom, Sergio Boixo, Ryan Babbush, Swarat Chaudhuri, and Pushmeet Kohli. We also thank Kevin Ishimwe, Ibrahim Alkhashem, and Matthew Harrigan for feedback and discussions on the Lean library, Emilien Dupont and Sebastian Nowozin for manuscript feedback, and Brendan Tracey for advice on the fusion application. Finally, we thank Uchechi Okereke, Ali Douraghy, and Andy Song for legal and policy support, and Alex Wilkins, Evie Gray, Danielle Breen, Dimple Vijaykumar, Muinat Abdul, Jason Freidenfelds, Chris Kwaku-Abdullahi, and Rob Ashley for their help with visuals and communicating this work.

title: Sharing catalog metadata across data platforms, engines, and agents
abstract: We’re excited to announce support for catalog labels – a new capability in the Apache Iceberg™ REST Catalog API that enables platforms, engines, and agents to access context such as business purpose, ownership and data classifications maintained in Iceberg REST-compatible catalogs. This shared context supports discovery, governance, and agentic workflows across the data and AI ecosystem. We believe that catalog metadata should be as open and portable as the data it describes. As enterprises bring more tools into their open lakehouse architectures, they need a common way to share the context that makes their data understandable, useful, and secure for all teams, regardless of what tools they use. Today, that context often remains siloed in the source catalog. Data and AI teams must recreate classifications across platforms, maintain custom metadata synchronization pipelines, or work with agents that lack complete context. Databricks is joined by Google Cloud, Salesforce, ClickHouse, Atlan, Collibra, DataHub, Immuta, Trust3 AI, PhoenixAI, and Datastrato in advancing this shared vision of metadata interoperability. Catalog labels offer a path toward that vision, making catalog context portable while allowing each platform to retain its own capabilities and controls. Databricks worked with the Apache Iceberg community to add an optional labels field to the Iceberg REST LoadTable response. This gives catalogs a standard way to expose table- and column-level context to other platforms, tools, and agents. Labels are string key-value pairs that can describe business ownership, intended use, sensitivity or other catalog-maintained context. The standard defines a common format for sharing this metadata without prescribing its vocabulary or interpretation, giving each platform the flexibility to build on it in its own way Consider a table named support_cases An authorized data steward assigns domain=customer_support and the Databricks system tag system.certification_status=certified to the table, and content_type=support_case_summary to the issue_summary column. A catalog exposing these tags could include the following in its Iceberg REST LoadTable response: This example shows only the labels portion of the response. A downstream platform can then use these labels to make the table more useful: This enables applications to inspect the table- and column- label labels from the same support_cases table. For example, PyIceberg has added support for accessing catalog labels in Python. In the next 0.13 release, applications will be able to inspect the table- and column-level labels from the same support_cases table: These labels make the catalog’s metadata available directly to Python applications, including data-discovery tools and agents. Unity Catalog exposes its table- and column-level tags through catalog labels with Tag Exchange. Tag Exchange is a step toward our broader vision of open governance: context maintained in one system should be usable across every platform, engine, and AI agent working with the data. By exposing Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags,Tag Exchange lets enterprises reuse classifications and business context for discovery, agent workflows, and access policies. Each tool has the freedom to decide how to interpret and use that context. Databricks is excited to join our partners in advancing catalog labels to make catalog metadata open and accessible. Together, we’re in support of an open interface that gives AI agents and data platforms shared context for discovering data, understanding it, and keeping it governed. Tag Exchange is available in Beta today, exposing Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags through catalog labels. To get started, enable “Tag Exchange via Iceberg REST Catalog” in the Databricks Previews portal. Catalog labels are string key-value pairs that share table- and column-level context through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. They can describe business ownership, intended use, sensitivity, and other metadata, helping platforms, tools, and agents understand the data they access. Databricks supports catalog labels through Tag Exchange, which exposes Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. External platforms, tools, and agents can use this context for discovery, classification, and locally defined access policies. Subscribe to our blog and get the latest posts delivered to your inbox.

title: What 5,400 Malicious npm Packages Reveal about Software Supply Chain Risk in 2026
abstract: This report is the first of a series of blogs analyzing the supply chain threat landscape. In this first part, we analyzed approximately 5,400 confirmed malicious npm packages published between December 2025 and October 2026, the first year following npm's revocation of long-lived authentication tokens [1]. Eight findings follow. The dataset comprises packages detected by our scanner, which analyzes npm publish events for suspicious packages, with results filtered for precision by retaining only packages with at least one independent source: a public advisory, a vendor-published campaign report, an npm security takedown, or analyst review. Time is measured by npm publish date. The unit of record is the package version; a package is dated by its first malicious version. Download counts are monthly snapshots recorded at scan time. Registry active status was checked against the public registry on November 6, 2026. Figure 1: Verdict Type by Month (%) Monthly counts of confirmed malicious packages vary by a factor of fifteen across the period. The variation is attributable to a small number of campaigns: in August 2026 a single dependency-confusion campaign accounts for 78% of confirmed versions. When each campaign is counted as a single actor, activity is stable: several hundred new publisher accounts per month, a flat rate of malicious packages relative to total packages published, and spikes attributable to named campaigns. Figure 2: Verified Malicious npm Packages by First-Publish Month Three changes are observable after this normalization: Compromise of legitimate packages is episodic. Activity is negligible in most months. Three waves of a single worm family occurred in May, June and August 2026; the May and August waves each compromised more than one hundred packages, and the June wave republished a vendor's entire scope in one day. Figure 3: Legitimate-Package Compromise, Poisoned Versions by Month Dependency-confusion reconnaissance is continuous , present in every month at a consistent level. Obfuscation increased. The share of actors whose packages trigger an obfuscation rule more than doubled between May and August 2026. Targeting of AI-developer credentials remained at 1-4% of packages throughout the year; absolute counts rose with volume. Theft of npm authentication tokens peaked at 22% of packages in March 2026 and fell below 5% from May. Classic long-lived tokens had been revoked on December 9, 2025; the tokens targeted in this period were plausibly granular access tokens and CI secrets. Figure 4: Share of Verified Packages Targeting Each Credential Class, by Month Figure 5: Cloud and AI-Dev Targeting: Packages vs. Actors (% of month) Figure 6: Profiles of Verified Malicious npm Publishing, May–October 2026 Publisher account. 99% of malicious packages are published by single-maintainer accounts; 55% of accounts use a free-mail address. Two thirds of accounts publish exactly one malicious package; among accounts publishing more than one, the median interval from first to last malicious publish is under one day. DPRK-nexus campaigns are the exception, operating several hundred accounts at one to two packages each, 83% on free-mail addresses. Other named campaigns use free-mail addresses in 15% of cases, consistent with procured account pools. Figure 7: Publisher accounts behind Verified Malicious npm Packages Package metadata. 88% of packages are under thirty days old at the malicious publish; 75% declare no repository; 66% have a single version; 65% retain npm init template values in the author, description or repository fields. 54% declare a lifecycle script. 17% carry an internal-looking name (core, utils, sdk, config). Typosquatting is a minority tactic: 13% embed a popular package name and under 5% are within two character edits of one. Figure 8: Author and Repository Spoofing in package.json file (%) Figure 9: Ecosystem Keywords Used in Malicious Package Names Compromise indicators. Compromised legitimate packages differ from attacker-created packages on the version-level change signals. 78% of compromised versions add or modify a lifecycle script, compared with 4% of attacker-created packages. 23% show a change of maintainer or publisher. The majority of compromises are published through the legitimate account and leave ownership records unchanged. Figure 10: Takeover Shape, Compromised Legitimate Packages vs Attacker-Published Behavior. 72% of packages have an obfuscation marker, and 30% retrieve a second stage. Credential and data theft is the predominant behavior in every month, except August. A significant number of packages in August stole credentials but ultimately aimed to deliver on the victim machine a Sliver command-and-control implant, changing its classification to Trojan / Downloader. Figure 11: Malware Packages by Behavior and Month Of credential stealers, 45% target a single credential class and 36% target three or more. Single-class stealers are distributed evenly across cloud credentials, SSH keys, AI-developer credentials, npm tokens and .env files. In multi-class stealers, cloud credentials, SSH keys and .env files co-occur; wallet and browser-data theft occur separately. AI-developer credentials are the most specialized target: 80% of packages that target them target no other class. Figure 12: Co-occurrence of credential classes Platform. 55% of packages contain no operating-system-specific code. Among the remainder, droppers target Windows (PowerShell, scheduled tasks, executables) and credential stealers and backdoors target Linux (systemd, cron, shell configuration files). macOS-specific code appears in approximately one in eight stealers. Lures. 24% of packages are scoped, across more than three hundred distinct scopes, most of which contain a single malicious package: an organization's internal namespace registered once. 36% declare an author and 24% a repository; where present, approximately 80% of each refer to an identity other than the publishing account. 62% include a README; of these, 16% contain an installation command for a different package, in half of those cases a popular one. The majority of attacker-created packages employ no lure, consistent with the exposure finding: these packages are retrieved by misconfigured builds rather than selected by users. Figure 14: Package-name lures (%) Compromised legitimate packages are 7% of the set and over 99% of its download exposure. Figure 15: Downloads per Month at Scan Time All compromise waves in the period belong to one family, first the toolkit of a single threat actor and later open-sourced for free use in May. The May and August worms each compromised more than one hundred packages. In June 2026 the same open-source kit republished a single vendor's entire scope in one day through trusted publishing, followed within days by a small number of unrelated packages. Outside these waves, compromise occurs at a rate of a few packages per month. Worm-compromised versions are distinguishable from attacker-created packages: all execute through a lifecycle script, one third read cloud credentials or the Kubernetes service-account token, and 44% trigger obfuscation rules. They receive public advisories within hours of publication. The August wave's highest-exposure victims were republished through OIDC trusted publishing from compromised CI environments rather than through stolen tokens. Across the period, 85% of packages in the malicious set published via trusted publishing are compromises. The December 2025 token revocation directed maintainers toward trusted publishing; subsequent compromise activity targeted the publishing pipeline directly. Shared legitimate services. 38% of packages, and 42% of those with a network indicator, communicate with a legitimate third-party service. Serverless hosting is most common; Cloudflare Workers alone serves several hundred packages from a comparable number of accounts.

title: Announcing General Availability of native Lakebase Postgres sink for Spark Structured Streaming
abstract: Low-latency use cases like fraud detection, live personalization, and real-time feature computation need computed results in a serving-ready OLTP store. Lakebase Postgres is Databricks' fully managed, serverless PostgreSQL database offering, with autoscaling, branching, native Unity Catalog integration, and sub 10ms reads. But writing to it from a streaming pipeline has meant building a custom foreach writer and handling batching, retries, and upserts yourself, which is complex to get right and hard to keep performant under load. Today, we are announcing the general availability of the native Lakebase sink for Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming, a connector that writes computed results directly to Lakebase and handles all of that for you. The same connector works in both micro-batch and Real-Time Mode . We show it on a feature pipeline that ingests watch and like events from a video streaming platform, computes each user's recent activity, and upserts one feature row per user into Lakebase in hundreds of milliseconds. You get that performance without building or maintaining the connector yourself. A foreach writer has to do a lot at once: batch writes for throughput, a bounded queue for backpressure, pool connections and refresh OAuth tokens, retry transient failures with backoff, deduplicate within a batch. It also has to implement upsert semantics correctly, including keeping the greatest timestamp or updating a column only when an incoming event has a newer ordering value. Even for an experienced developer, writing and tuning all of this is weeks of work, and it does not end there. The connector turns into something you maintain, fixing throughput regressions, credential refresh, and keeping the code current with the latest versions. For a sense of what that looks like in practice, see this reference implementation . The native sink takes care of it. You wire up a Lakebase write in minutes with a single writeStream call, and spend no time on performance, tuning, or maintaining the connector. You get: A video streaming provider wants to recommend videos to its viewers. A recommendation model needs what users watched most recently. So for each user we compute the last 6 videos they watched and the last 3 they liked. We store that as one row per user in Lakebase. At inference time, the recommendation model looks up that row by user_id to rank what to show next. A feature is an input the model uses to make a prediction. Here, the features are each user's recent activity, computed from a stream of events. Each event has a user_id and a video_id and an event type (WATCH/LIKE). For each user we keep their recent watches and likes as one row, keyed by user_id . Every new event for a user_id updates that row in place. Writing to Lakebase is a single writeStream call. How you point it at Lakebase depends on whether the target table is registered in Unity Catalog. If the Lakebase table is registered in Unity Catalog , write with .toTable() using the fully qualified catalog.schema.table . The connector manages credentials as the running user or service principal, and creates the table if it doesn't exist: If the Lakebase table isn't registered in Unity Catalog, write to the Lakebase endpoint directly with format("postgresql") (see Lakebase tables not registered with Unity Catalog ). The same format("postgresql") path also supports writing to external PostgreSQL databases (e.g. Amazon RDS or self-hosted) via a Unity Catalog connection (DBR 19+, Public Preview). The sink writes the features into Lakebase within 100-200 milliseconds of being produced, with no offline-to-online sync in between. Applications and models can query them in single-digit milliseconds. This supports two patterns: For a deeper look at the implementation, see the companion repo , a self-serve example you can run end-to-end. We ran the pipeline at a sustained input rate of ~20K events/sec against 5 million active users, each accumulating watch and like history. The cluster used was a 40-core classic compute (DBR 18 LTS) writing to an 8-CU Lakebase project with 5-minute RTM checkpoint intervals. Every event is an upsert that overwrites that user's existing feature row in Lakebase. As state builds up, the sink is continuously upserting against a table with millions of existing rows, finding and replacing the row for each user_id on every event. This is the workload pattern that breaks custom foreach writers at scale. End-to-end latency is measured from the Kafka input timestamp to the row landing in Lakebase. 20k Events per sec (1 hour sustained) Active user (state cardinality) Note: This illustrative example uses synthetic data replayed into Kafka. The test ran for 60 minutes, achieving ~20K EPS and 63.5 million upserts. These latencies are specific to this setup. Your numbers will differ with input rate, the amount of state you keep, RTM cluster size, and Lakebase size. Size both the cluster and Lakebase to sustain the throughput you need. The sink also lets you tune how it batches writes using batchinterval and batchsize . See performance tuning . At this throughput on an 8-CU project, pg_stat_statements shows 63.5 million upserts averaging ~0.015 milliseconds per statement. Lakebase had headroom to spare. For a deeper look at how Lakebase achieves this, see the blog, How Lakebase Architecture Delivers 5x Faster Postgres Writes . With Real-Time Mode computing features as events arrive and the native Lakebase sink enabling writes directly to a serving-ready OLTP database, together they unblock real-time feature computation and ingestion in one streaming pipeline. The native sink gives you a first-class experience when writing to Lakebase, using the same writeStream API you already know. We showed it on a recommendation feature pipeline, but the same pattern works wherever a streaming pipeline needs to write computed results to a database for immediate serving. The native Lakebase sink for Spark Structured Streaming is now Generally Available. What is the native Lakebase sink for Spark Structured Streaming? It’s a Structured Streaming connector that writes computed results directly to Lakebase. It handles batching, retries, connection pooling, deduplication, upserts, and workspace-managed authentication, so you don’t build a custom foreach writer. The same connector works in both micro-batch and Real-Time Mode. Is the native Lakebase sink generally available? Yes. The native Lakebase sink for Spark Structured Streaming is now generally available on Databricks Runtime 18 LTS and above. The RealTime and ProcessingTime triggers run on classic compute; on serverless, use Trigger.AvailableNow . It isn’t supported in Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines. How do I write to Lakebase with the sink? For a Lakebase table registered in Unity Catalog, use .toTable() with the fully qualified catalog.schema.table ; the connector manages credentials and creates the table if it doesn’t exist. For an unregistered table, use format("postgresql") with the Lakebase endpoint and dbtable . Does the sink support upserts and custom merge logic? Yes. Declare an upsertkey and the sink maintains one row per key. Merge strategies (DBR 19+) control how non-key columns update on conflict, such as keeping the latest non-null value or the value from the newest event, with no hand-written ON CONFLICT SQL. What use cases is the native Lakebase sink built for? The native Lakebase sink is built for operational dashboards, app databases, and low-latency feature stores.. Examples include real-time feature computation for recommendations and personalization, and fraud detection. Subscribe to our blog and get the latest posts delivered to your inbox.

title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
abstract: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today. Without intervention, kids in Virginia and Oregon risk a lifetime of distress, as Grok images will likely be impossible to remove online. “Once created and shared,” Grok-generated CSAM and NCII “can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child’s abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child’s life,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ complaint said. “Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm.” Millions allegedly harmed Millions of residents were allegedly harmed, as the attorneys general seek to protect every Grok or X user in their state. Many Grok victims will likely suffer from chronic anxiety, depression, and PTSD, as well as reputational harm, as some viewers may not realize the images are AI-generated, the states alleged. Further—due to Grok’s integration with the social media platform X—users as young as 13 may have been exposed to the AI content and possibly re-traumatized if they, too, are victims of sexual abuse, the states alleged.

title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
abstract: Nvidia’s board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals . The reinstatement, announced Monday morning , is “effective immediately” and was based in part on “input from senior levels of the United States government” that assured the board members that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” That assurance comes despite Huang’s admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures. Huang had been seeking a return to Nvidia since shortly after his resignation, reportedly forming a war room to strategize how best to bring it to pass. Last week, Huang posted on social media that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” President Trump has also been a major backer of Huang’s return to Nvidia. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” he wrote on Truth Social last week. “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” In a social media post immediately following the reinstatement, Trump called it “the correct and proper decision” and confirmed that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” Appearing on CNBC Monday morning , Trump said that he had spoken to the Nvidia board “directly and indirectly” about Huang’s reinstatement, and that Huang “did nothing wrong.” Losing “the brainpower of someone like [Huang]” would be “a much bigger threat” than anything related to his alleged interactions with China, Trump said.

title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
abstract: Buying a new computer in the last few years has meant wading through all manner of AI branding nonsense . Most of the AI pitches for laptops are little more than marketing hype, but the launch of Nvidia RTX Spark could bring a meaningful improvement in AI capabilities to the device you use every day. Asus has adopted Nvidia's new chip in its latest ProArt lineup, offering a staggering amount of memory to run local AI models. While it doesn't have a traditional GPU, the Asus ProArt P16 , with up to 128GB of memory, can also be your primary gaming and productivity machine, but this unified experience comes at a high price. If you want to run a small army of agents on your laptop, you're looking at $7,000 for the top-end ProArt P16, and despite being more approachable on Windows, local AI still requires a lot of trial and error. Before we dive into the AI agents, let's talk about the ProArt P16 as a laptop. Nvidia's pitch is that the RTX Spark can be your one true machine for AI, productivity, and gaming. And it doesn't skimp on the specs.

title: Ladybird’s first alpha release
abstract: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components—things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird’s even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I’ve been trying it out today, and it’s very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I’ve tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool): Here’s the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script , thanks Claude): Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site). I tried Ladybird against several of my more advanced tool examples—like the video-compressor shown above, which runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. I had it resize its own screenshot using my image-resize tool . It happily runs my Pyodide REPL (Python compiled to WebAssembly) too. The one thing I tried that didn’t work was Datasette Lite , which runs Pyodide in a complicated arrangement of service workers and web workers. Attempting to start Datasette Lite displays this error: undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages') I filed an issue about this , then found a FIXME annotation in the source code. The project has been leaning heavily into coding agents this year. On February 23, 2026 Andreas Kling published Ladybird adopts Rust, with help from AI , describing how they ported parts of their LibJS JavaScript engine from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex. Here’s the GitHub contributions chart for Ladybird over the past twelve months: That uptick in October corresponds to the landing of a wealth of big improvements. This Month in Ladybird — October 2026 describes what happened. In addition to moving style and layout to their own thread, landing a new JavaScript JIT, and replacing their C++ with Cranelift WebAssembly engine with new code that achieved a 7x boost on the JetStream 3 WASM benchmark , they gained 75,650 new passes on the ~2.25 million subtest web-platform-tests suite, beating Safari! How did they do that? Coding agents: Most of that gain came in five days, from about 2.12 million on October 22 to about 2.18 million on October 27. We pointed AI coding agents at WPT and asked them to fill in missing functionality. They made lots of small fixes, and those added up. Our biggest gains for the month were about 30,000 in /css and 10,000 in /editing . I’m interested in what models they are using here—I know Andreas uses Codex and Claude Code, but I haven’t seen him talk about specific model versions. Claude Opus 5.5 came out on September 22, 2026 and Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026 (after that window). I’d love to know what they were using for that huge leap in the last week of October. Here’s what Andreas says about Ladybird’s suitability for use as a daily browser: This is an alpha, so some websites won’t work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it. Our privacy policy has the details. We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today. When you pwn us, please tell us how so we can harden Ladybird! Given how hard it is to secure a web browser, and the hostility of the environment they operate in, I won’t be using Ladybird to sign into GitHub or Gmail or any of my other sensitive accounts. I’m going to keep it around for anonymous browsing though, partly to participate in the testing efforts but mainly because it gives me a glimmer of optimism to see a promising new entrant in the stagnant browser engine market start to grow its wings. This is Ladybird’s first alpha release by Simon Willison, posted on 23rd November 2026 . title: samuelgursky/davinci-resolve-mcp
abstract:
DaVinci Resolve MCP Server English | 簡體中文 | 繁體中文 A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI assistants control DaVinci Resolve Studio through the official Scripting API. It provides full API coverage plus guarded workflow helpers for editing, media pool organization, render setup, review markers, grading, Fusion, Fairlight, project lifecycle tasks, extension authoring, and source-safe media analysis. A local browser control panel ships with the server for inspecting Resolve state, running source-safe analysis, drilling into analyzed clips and shots, and editing analysis output inline. See the Control Panel Guide for the full tour. Quick Start npx davinci-resolve-mcp setup Before connecting, open DaVinci Resolve Studio and set Preferences > General > External scripting using to Local . (On the free edition that preference does not help — see Free edition below.) The npm launcher installs a managed copy under your user application-data directory, then runs the universal Python installer. The installer creates a virtual environment, detects Resolve paths, and can configure Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Continue, Cline, Roo Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, and JetBrains IDEs. For source installs: git clone https://github.com/samuelgursky/davinci-resolve-mcp.git cd davinci-resolve-mcp
python install.py For platform paths, client-specific config, and manual setup, see Installation and Configuration . The installer and server check the latest GitHub release for MCP updates. Checks are best-effort and throttled; the server never blocks MCP startup for a prompt. The installer can prompt, snooze, ignore a release, disable checks, or apply an opt-in safe auto-update for clean git checkouts. Free edition (in-app bridge) Blackmagic gates external scripting to Studio: on the free edition scriptapp("Resolve") refuses a foreign process, whatever the preference says.
Through Resolve 21.0.x the Workspace ▸ Scripts menu was not gated — a script
launched from it is handed the live resolve object (measured on free 21.0.3.7) —
so the server can reach the free edition through a small script that runs inside Resolve and re-exports it over an authenticated loopback listener. Resolve 21.1
moved Python scripting to Studio. On free 21.1 the Scripts menu no longer lists .py files at all (reported on Fedora 44 in #203; a Lua script in the same folder
lists normally). Whether the Console still runs Python there is unconfirmed, so
treat the bridge as a 21.0.x path until that is measured. python scripts/install_resolve_bridge.py # restart Resolve, open a project, then: Workspace > Scripts > resolve_bridge The installer and MCP client use ~/.config/davinci-resolve-mcp/bridge.json by default. To keep the authenticated bridge config elsewhere, set DAVINCI_RESOLVE_BRIDGE_CONFIG while running the installer and in the MCP
client environment; both sides will use that path. Once that listener is running it is used automatically whenever external
scripting is unavailable — no environment variable required. Setting DAVINCI_RESOLVE_BRIDGE=1 forces the bridge instead: it becomes the only
transport tried, so a bridge that stops answering reports its own fault rather
than quietly falling back to another transport. Use it when the bridge is the
path you intend to depend on. On macOS , Resolve looks for Python 3 in exactly two places: the PYTHON3HOME environment variable, then /usr/local/bin/python3 . Homebrew,
pyenv, uv and conda land in neither, so the script silently never appears in the
menu. A python.org install works because its installer creates /usr/local/bin/python3 — but you do not need one: point Resolve at the
interpreter you already have, no sudo required. launchctl setenv PYTHON3HOME " $( python3 -c ' import sys; print(sys.prefix) ' ) " Use launchctl setenv , not export — Resolve is launched from the Dock and
never sees your shell's environment. Restart Resolve afterwards. A Lua canary is
installed alongside so you can tell "Python not detected" apart from a wrong
folder. Two things that bite (#182). The prefix must contain both lib/libpython3.X.dylib and bin/python3 under that exact unversioned name — Homebrew's framework builds often ship only bin/python3.13 , which is
half a Python as far as Resolve is concerned, and the installer's preflight now
says so instead of reporting a usable prefix. And launchctl setenv does not
survive a reboot ; if scripts stop listing weeks later with no error, that is
why. For something persistent, put an interpreter where Resolve already looks
(this one needs sudo , and check that /usr/local/bin does not precede your
normal Python on PATH ): sudo ln -s " $( command -v python3 ) " /usr/local/bin/python3 Validated on free 21.0.3.7 and Studio 19.1.3.7, both macOS. The Windows paths
added in v2.70.1 (issue #106) shipped unverified; reports on free 21.0.1.11
(issue #109) and free 21.0.3.7 (issue #112) have since shown the bridge
installing, listing and serving from both %PROGRAMDATA% and %APPDATA% on
Windows 11, so those paths are now confirmed rather than assumed. Linux is
confirmed as well: a report on free 20.3.2.9 (issue #129, Fedora 43) shows the
bridge installing to ~/.local/share/DaVinciResolve/Fusion/Scripts/Utility ,
listing against the system Python — Linux has none of this discovery problem —
and serving end-to-end. No platform now rests on an assumption: macOS was
validated directly, Windows and Linux on user reports. Note that the bridge holds its port for as long as it serves. Before v2.70.3 a
Windows bridge could outlive Resolve and block the next session's listener; if
you are on an older build and a bridge stops answering, check for a stale fuscript.exe still holding the port. This is the documented in-app path, not a licence circumvention, but Blackmagic
could close it — treat it as a supported-until-it-is-not tier. Loopback only,
HMAC-signed requests, one-use nonces. Local Control Panel Launch the single-user local control panel from the repository root: venv/bin/python -m src.control_panel The command starts a loopback-only server and opens the control panel in your browser at a URL that carries a per-launch access token ( http://127.0.0.1:8765/#token=… ) — use that exact URL; the panel refuses requests without it. To have an AI coding agent do this, ask: "Open the Resolve MCP control panel for this repo." Agents should use venv/bin/python -m src.control_panel unless your Python environment is already active. Persisted analysis jobs refresh the local search index automatically after successful slices; the manual Build Index action is for rebuilding from existing reports. Server Modes Mode Entry point Tools Best for Compound src/server.py 37 Default mode for most assistants. Related Resolve operations are grouped behind action parameters to keep context usage low. Full / granular src/server.py --full or src/resolve_mcp_server.py 390 Power users who want one MCP tool per Resolve API method. The compound server is recommended unless you specifically need the granular one-tool-per-method surface. Advanced server — beyond the scripting API (optional, Node) The same package ships a second, optional MCP server: davinci-resolve-advanced-mcp (bin bin/davinci-resolve-advanced-mcp.mjs ). Where the Python server drives a live Resolve over the
sanctioned scripting API, the advanced server does what the API can't — it reads and edits Resolve files ( .drp / .drt / .drx ) and applies DB/XML-level changes with no Resolve running , so it
runs cloud or local.

title: Apple removed my open-source app from EU App Stores after 9 years
abstract:
Apple Removed FSNotes from European App Stores After 9 Years — and Has Ignored My Support Requests #2056 glushchenko started this conversation in General Apple Removed FSNotes from European App Stores After 9 Years — and Has Ignored My Support Requests #2056 glushchenko Nov 23, 2026 · 1 comment Return to top Discussion options Uh oh! There was an error while loading. Please reload this page . Quote reply edited Uh oh! There was an error while loading. Please reload this page . glushchenko Nov 23, 2026 Maintainer Hi everyone! For those who don't know me, let me introduce myself. I'm the independent developer behind FSNotes , an open-source note-taking app for macOS and iOS. I've been developing FSNotes for 9 years. And what happened a few weeks ago came as a complete shock. Apple removed my app from every European App Store. Without a clear explanation or any way to resolve the issue promptly. It all started when I didn't receive my October sales payout. This had happened before, but I was usually able to resolve it by contacting Apple Support. Not this time. I opened two support cases: November 5 — Case ID: 23353628 November 17 — Case ID: 23573022 Since November 5, I haven't received a single response. Not one. I've gone through everything I could find in App Store Connect, completed the necessary compliance information under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA), and submitted official documents from Ukraine's government business registry. I'm a legally registered sole proprietor in Ukraine. I run my business officially and pay my taxes. But apparently, that's not enough. Or perhaps nobody is even reviewing my documents. And you know what's the most frustrating part? While Apple remains silent, everything I've spent nine years building is being destroyed. My app is losing its positions in App Store rankings and search results. The visibility, reputation, and discoverability I've worked so hard to build over the years are disappearing right before my eyes. Even if Apple restores my app tomorrow, who's going to give me those rankings back? Who will compensate me for the lost time, users, and revenue? I'm not asking for special treatment. I'm not asking Apple to bend the rules for me. I simply want someone to review my documents, explain the restrictions, and give me a chance to resolve the issue. It's especially painful to see how difficult it has become for a Ukrainian developer to keep working. Sometimes it feels like Ukraine is the country under sanctions, not Russia. FSNotes is still available for free on GitHub. I'll continue providing access to the source code and free builds. But the reality is that without revenue, it will be extremely difficult for an independent project like this to survive. I'm asking you to support this open letter to Apple with a like or a repost. I'm not asking for donations or special privileges. I just want to bring this situation to the attention of the App Store team. You cannot simply remove an app with a nine-year history from sale, ignore a developer's support requests for weeks, and provide no explanation of what's happening. This kind of treatment is killing indie development. Apple, please listen. title: Kagi Mail (public beta)
abstract:
We are proud to announce something that our small team of very dedicated people at Kagi has been building for a long time – the public beta of Kagi Mail . A private email and calendar with a @kagimail.com address, or with your own domains. If you’ve already swapped Google Search for Kagi and Chrome for Orion, your inbox is probably the last big piece of your digital life still at Google. Now you can move that too. Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days $99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate. Why we built it Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once. There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way . For email, that job is to be fast, private, and secure. On top of that, it should help you stay on track with what’s important: bring forward what you need to act on, respond to, or acknowledge, and quietly handle the rest. Kagi Mail also has to treat you the way Kagi Search and Orion do: no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in. Already a Kagi member? Kagi Mail is included in Ultimate . Sign in with your Kagi account, and you’re set. AI features draw from your existing Allowance. On another plan, or no Kagi account yet? After the free 60-day trial, you can get Kagi Mail for $99/year (+ Sales Tax). How it works: A service and a client, on open standards To deliver the experience we believe in, we built the full stack: hosting for your addresses and domains, plus the mail and calendar apps. It runs on open standards and open-source infrastructure (the Stalwart server, IMAP, JMAP, and CalDAV), so you can use Kagi’s apps or any compatible client you already like. The basics A @kagimail.com address Unlimited aliases Unlimited domains Built-in Calendar 50 GB of storage Intelligence Organize your mail in your own words. Brief it the way you’d brief an assistant: “Label anything where beta users send product feedback. It might come from @kagimail.com, but use judgment.” You decide what permissions each rule gets (read the content, or skip the inbox). Inbox Highlights show what needs you today, and learn from what you dismiss. Ask your inbox in plain language and get direct answers with the source email, including text inside scanned PDFs and photos. Newsletter view reads newsletters like a feed, out of the way of real mail. Responsible AI, with one switch to turn it all off. You control what AI is allowed to do and infer . Private by default Tracking pixels and remote images are blocked or proxied, so senders can’t tell when or where you opened their mail. Sender screening holds new senders until you approve them, so they never reach your inbox uninvited. Suspicious senders trigger a phishing warning, while verified senders show their (BMI) logo. No ads, ever. No profiling, no selling, no sharing your data. For teams and families Shared addresses on your domain (team@, info@, family@): create an alias, then choose which people have access to it Sign in through a social login, or your organization’s own identity provider (OIDC) Coming soon: Shared mailboxes Kagi integration Kagi Translate is built in Email Assistant: Write to assistant@kagimail.com for answers about your mail (actions coming soon) Proofread and translation included while you write emails For power users and developers Keyboard-first: command palette, shortcuts, and search operators Rule-based filtering with Sieve, no AI involved MCP server with read access to your mail Works with Apple Mail, Thunderbird, and any IMAP/JMAP/CalDAV client, with automatic setup What’s not here yet We will keep adding new capabilities – here’s what to expect over the next few quarters. Feature Target Contacts and address book Q1 2027 Full Kagi Assistant integration Q1 2027 Native mobile apps Q3 2027 Until the mobile apps arrive, use the mobile web app or any IMAP/JMAP client, such as Apple Mail or Thunderbird. Our “no lock-in” promise to you Leaving Kagi Mail is as easy as joining it. Your mail, calendar, and workflows are yours, and you can export them at any time, through standard protocols and a one-click export experience. You’ll keep access to your mailbox for six months after leaving Kagi Mail. You can send and receive emails for the first 60 days, then read and export your mail with one click for the remaining four months. We build an ecosystem so things work better together for those who want it, not to trap anyone . Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days $99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate. We want Kagi Mail to be the first email account we’d create for our children. We’re not there yet, but it is a high bar we hold ourselves to, and every feature in this beta is a step toward it: a calm, safe place to communicate, and a window onto an internet that treats you as a person, not a product who’s been tracked, targeted, and sold to. We can build it this way because of you. Kagi has no ad business, and no one pushing us to monetize your inbox; you’re not a dataset for ads or AI. You are here because you believe the internet can be built differently. Thank you.

title: CoMotion: A Real-Time System for User-Driven Semantic Steering in Text-to-Motion Generation
abstract: Current text-to-motion frameworks typically operate as a rigid, one-shot workflow where users are unable to intervene during the generation process, effectively limiting all refinement efforts to the iterative modification of the text prompt. This black-box process hinders iterative design, leading to inefficiency. Furthermore, natural language inherently suffers from ambiguity when describing fine-grained 3D motions, making it difficult for users to articulate their intent solely through text precisely. In this paper, we propose CoMotion, a real-time system that shifts the interaction paradigm from static text prompting to user-driven semantic steering. Instead of requiring users to restart the entire generation process for every modification, CoMotion operates directly within a discrete latent space by retrieving prompt-relevant atomic actions and presenting them as user-visible, adjustable controls. Through CoMotion, users can adjust semantic steering levels for these atomic actions to guide the generation toward their intent without the computational overhead of full text-to-motion model re-inference. Our approach provides a more diverse design pathway for the traditional one-shot text-to-motion generation process, enabling fine-grained, personalized motion control during generation. We validate our system using a standardized benchmark based on Large Language Models. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that CoMotion enables robust semantic correction and geometric diversity while maintaining the kinematic quality of the generated motions. Crucially, by transforming complex generative tasks into low-latency, interactive operations, CoMotion supports an interactive refinement workflow for the evaluated motion generation tasks.

title: Foundations for MetNet: A Proposed Framework for Modeling Metaphorical Productivity
abstract: Abstract An adequate computational treatment of metaphor requires a representational model that captures its cross-domain, productive nature. Existing approaches and resources fall short: (i) ontological models of general meaning representation, such as WordNet, ConceptNet, BabelNet, and OntoLex, treat concepts atomically, omitting the event structure needed to capture contextual variation; (ii) distributional models (e.g., Word2Vec, BERT) encode metaphorical patterns only implicitly, offering little interpretive insight; (iii) metaphor-specific resources such as MetaNet typically pre-encode mappings rather than deriving them from independent structure, or emphasize ontological (Framester, Amnestic Forgery) or pragmatic (MetCL) representation instead. Although FrameNet – encoding events (frames) and participant roles (frame elements) to support systematic cross-domain alignment – offers a promising foundation, existing approaches built on it leave the underlying linguistic mechanism unaccounted for. In this paper, we review these models and resources to motivate the need for a new theoretical approach to capture this linguistic – and thus systemic – metaphorical mechanism, MetNet, a theoretical framework that refines FrameNet for metaphor modeling through a dedicated reasoning engine, specified through four core tenets: lexical frames, providing the structured, role-based representations over which mappings are established; abstract frames, narrowing the space of plausible candidate pairs; constraints, determining whether a given candidate mapping is admissible; and a mappability scale, grading admitted mappings by the density of their preserved relational structure. Our approach rests on two premises: (i) metaphor should be modeled analogically, as mappings between non-metaphorical frames; and (ii) evaluating such mappings requires a framework capable of encoding graded alignment constraints.

title: VsensAgent: A Human-Agent Interface for Collaborative Virtual Sensor Data Authoring
abstract: Virtual sensing can reduce the cost of generating sensor datasets for human activity recognition and ubiquitous sensing, yet users must still translate sensing intent into concrete scene configurations. This fragmentation makes it difficult to translate sensing goals into concrete configurations and refine them as results emerge. We present VsensAgent, a human–agent interface that grounds an LLM-powered agent in a shared 3D simulation environment. Users combine natural-language delegation with direct scene manipulation, while the agent can inspect scene state, configure sensors and avatar motions, record data, and support signal analysis. We conducted a task-based study of VsensAgent in which 12 participants completed 36 virtual sensing authoring sessions. Analysis of interaction logs, authored configurations, and post-task interviews showed that participants progressively developed intent through executable scene states, shifted control between agent delegation and direct manipulation at the level of individual operations, and treated agent proposals as editable starting points. These findings frame virtual sensor generation as progressive, collaborative authoring and inform the design of agents for stateful workflows.
